auto-23e4645ed453.headline: North Korea launches unidentified projectile into the sea, South Korea says
auto-23e4645ed453.summary: North Korea fired an unidentified projectile toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan, on Thursday, according to South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff. The military announced the launch around 12:40 p.m. local time but had not yet given the launch location. Japan's Coast Guard separately reported a suspected ballistic missile about a minute earlier and said it appeared to have landed within minutes, suggesting a short-range missile. Details beyond these initial reports were not yet available.

actors.why: Launch detected by its military; direct security threat near its waters
Coast Guard reported suspected ballistic missile; regional threat to Japan
Launched the projectile; no costs or sanctions described in the article

impact_points: South Korea and Japan face a fresh North Korean missile launch that heightens regional security concerns.
Regional neighbours and allies must assess the threat as the projectile's type and target remain unconfirmed.

auto-a875d48c28e0.headline: Drone strike damages container ship off Bulgarian Black Sea coast, crew rescued
auto-a875d48c28e0.summary: A container vessel was struck by a drone in waters off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. Everyone aboard was pulled to safety, with no crew members left unaccounted for. The incident adds to concerns about attacks on commercial shipping in the region's busy waters.

actors.why: Attack occurred in Bulgarian coastal waters; crew rescued, security concerns rise
Regional drone attacks on shipping are linked to the wider Black Sea conflict

impact_points: Bulgaria faces a security incident on its coastline, raising concern about maritime safety in its waters.
Shipping operators and crews in the Black Sea face heightened risk from drone attacks on commercial vessels.

auto-7b892ca421f1.headline: North Korea launches around ten ballistic missiles toward eastern waters
auto-7b892ca421f1.summary: North Korea fired roughly ten to a dozen short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on Thursday, according to South Korea's military. The launch took place from the Wonsan area around 12:30 p.m. local time. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said it was still analysing the missiles' flight distances and other specifications. It is the latest launch after a test on October 12 that Pyongyang described as tactical missiles meant to improve a key weapons component. Seoul said it has increased surveillance and is coordinating closely with Washington and Tokyo.

actors.why: Fires missiles, advancing its weapons programme while drawing regional alarm
Faces a new missile threat and must heighten surveillance and defences
Coordinates closely with Seoul on the launch, raising alliance security concerns
Shares launch information with Seoul and faces regional missile risks

impact_points: South Korea faces heightened security concerns and is boosting surveillance and defensive readiness after the launch.
The United States and Japan are being kept informed through close information-sharing as regional military tensions continue.

auto-346eafc5b741.headline: El Salvador deploys about 1,000 troops to Haiti after four peacekeepers vanish
auto-346eafc5b741.summary: El Salvador has flown roughly 1,000 soldiers into Haiti, a major expansion of its role in the country's gang crisis. The deployment follows an October 18 ambush on the edge of the capital that left four Salvadoran members of a UN-backed security mission missing. A Haitian security official confirmed the arrivals to Reuters, speaking anonymously. It is still unclear who will lead the new contingent, how long it will remain, or whether further forces will be sent. Officials in Haiti and El Salvador had not responded to requests for comment.

actors.why: Sends about 1,000 troops after four nationals went missing in ambush
Gains major reinforcements against gangs amid escalating violence in capital

impact_points: El Salvador is committing a large military force to Haiti, raising its exposure and the operational burden on its army.
Haiti is gaining substantial reinforcements in its fight against armed gangs, though the mission's duration and command remain uncertain.

auto-4a7ce6a9ff42.headline: Putin hosts African leaders in Moscow to deepen Russia's continental ties
auto-4a7ce6a9ff42.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin opened a two-day summit in Moscow with delegations from 48 countries, including 22 African leaders. He argued that Russia is Africa's best partner and criticised Western powers for exploiting the continent's resources and using debt to slow its development. Putin called for African states to have a bigger say at the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. The summit, the third of its kind, is co-chaired by the African Union's current chair, Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye, who said African countries want to move beyond exporting raw materials. More than 40 sessions are planned on trade, energy, food security and other areas.

actors.why: Hosts summit to expand influence, positioning itself as Africa's preferred partner
Burundi's president co-chairs the summit as current African Union chair
Criticised by Putin as exploiting Africa's resources and debt, facing rising Russian competition
Implicitly targeted by Putin's criticism of Western domination in former colonial markets

impact_points: Russia gains a platform to widen its political, economic and military footprint across Africa, where its Africa Corps fighters operate.
African states seek leverage over global lenders and better value from their resources, while Western powers face sharper competition for influence.

auto-7dc0a335feb0.headline: US sanctions ten North Korean and Russian nationals over IT worker fraud
auto-7dc0a335feb0.summary: The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control has imposed sanctions on ten individuals and entities linked to schemes that place North Korean IT workers at American companies under false identities. Eight of the designated people are North Korean, two are Russian, and one is a Pyongyang-controlled entity. Officials said the operations defraud US businesses and channel revenue to North Korea's weapons programmes. The sanctions were announced in a press release on Wednesday, and two North Korean individuals, Kim Ki Hyok and Kim Hyo Dong, were named for supporting a company already under US sanctions.

actors.why: Eight citizens and a state-linked entity sanctioned over revenue-generating IT worker schemes
Two Russian nationals sanctioned for helping North Korean workers obtain jobs
Sanctions enforcement against revenue flows to North Korean weapons programmes

impact_points: North Korea faces tighter US financial restrictions tied to revenue that officials say funds its weapons programmes.
Russia sees two of its nationals sanctioned, adding pressure on Moscow-linked facilitators of the fraud scheme.

auto-e61f3f8c85ff.headline: Israeli strikes and fire in Gaza leave at least four Palestinians dead
auto-e61f3f8c85ff.summary: Israeli attacks across Gaza have reportedly killed at least four Palestinians and wounded more than 30, according to the Iranian outlet Mehr News. One death came from wounds sustained in an Israeli strike on a checkpoint in al-Mawasi, southern Gaza, an area where tens of thousands of displaced people live in tents and which Israel had earlier designated a safe zone. Separately, artillery reportedly struck a house east of Gaza City, injuring 11 people including women and children, and an air strike hit an empty apartment block in the Bureij camp in central Gaza with no injuries reported. Additional artillery fire was also reported near Jabaliya in northern Gaza.

actors.why: Civilians killed and wounded across several Gaza areas by strikes and artillery
Israeli forces are carrying out the attacks reported across Gaza

impact_points: Palestinian civilians in Gaza, including displaced families in al-Mawasi, face continued deadly fire and casualties.
Israel faces renewed scrutiny over strikes in areas it had designated as safe zones for civilians.

auto-cdaf97778c07.headline: Russian missile strike injures five in Kharkiv region town
auto-cdaf97778c07.summary: A Russian missile attack hit the town of Derhachi in Kharkiv Oblast in Ukraine on Tuesday, 27 October, according to the regional military administration head, Oleh Syniehubov. Three people were initially reported injured, and he later said two more had sought medical care. A warehouse building was struck, and petrol station equipment and a car were damaged. Emergency services were handling the aftermath, and medics were treating the wounded.

actors.why: Civilians injured and property damaged in a Russian missile strike on Derhachi
Its missile strike caused injuries and damage in a Ukrainian town

impact_points: Ukraine's Kharkiv region faces fresh civilian casualties and damage to local infrastructure from the Russian strike.
Russia's continued missile strikes on Ukrainian towns keep pressure on local emergency services and residents.

auto-7836901f5597.headline: US defence chief pitches Asean security framework amid regional scepticism
auto-7836901f5597.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has proposed a new defence framework between the United States and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations while visiting the Philippines. A question from a reporter pressed him on what Southeast Asian states are contributing to America's strategic priorities. Analysts quoted in the piece doubt the plan will yield a broad, bloc-wide arrangement. They point to Asean's longstanding reluctance to take sides between Washington and Beijing and to the constraints of its consensus-driven decision-making.

actors.why: Hosts the talks and gains closer US defence engagement, though faces pressure to deliver
Pitches the framework but may struggle to secure tangible returns from partners
Not directly involved in the framework discussions

impact_points: The Philippines and other Asean members face pressure to show concrete returns from closer US defence ties.
Washington wants tangible gains, while Asean's bloc-wide consensus model may stall any sweeping security arrangement.

auto-c44e15a66d80.headline: Russia says it downed a record 1,214 Ukrainian drones in one night
auto-c44e15a66d80.summary:
Russia's Defense Ministry reported that its air defenses intercepted 1,214 Ukrainian drones overnight, a new record that tops the previous high set in September. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 613 drones were sent toward the capital region, with about a third destroyed on approach. The Kremlin condemned the attack as talks between the two sides are being planned for next month under U.S. mediation.

Debris caused minor damage at an industrial site in Sterlitamak, where an exiled outlet said the target was a chemical plant that is Russia's only producer of a material used in body armor. Governors in Perm and Belgorod also reported damage and casualties, with one person killed in Belgorod. Ukrainian officials separately said a Russian strike in Rivne killed one person.

actors.why: Record drone barrage hit Moscow region and industrial sites, causing casualties and damage.
Ukraine launched the drone wave and Russia says it was intercepted; Ukraine also reports a Russian strike death.
Washington is mediating the upcoming peace talks between Russia and Ukraine.

impact_points: Russia faces strikes on industrial sites and a chemical plant key to military protective materials.
Ukraine and Russia both face casualties while peace negotiations are being prepared.

auto-5b274b3deeed.headline: US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry over alleged backing of Congo rebels
auto-5b274b3deeed.summary: The United States has placed sanctions on Rwanda's ministry of defence, accusing it of helping keep the M23 rebel group active in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Washington also sanctioned Zigama Credit and Savings Society, which it says helps channel Rwandan support to the rebels. The US Treasury says Rwandan troops fought alongside M23 and supplied equipment and training. Kigali has repeatedly denied backing the group, while Kinshasa has welcomed the measures. The move follows a US-brokered peace deal between the two countries that has so far changed little on the ground.

actors.why: Defence ministry and a credit society hit by US sanctions over alleged rebel support
Gains US pressure on Rwanda while fighting with M23 continues
Uses sanctions to press Kigali to honour the Washington peace accords

impact_points: Rwanda faces US financial penalties and pressure to pull its troops out of eastern Congo.
The Democratic Republic of Congo gains US backing in its push to end M23 control of key eastern areas.

auto-932b32bb9a8a.headline: Russian drone strike on Dnipro rail platform kills 13, injures at least five
auto-932b32bb9a8a.summary:
A jet-powered drone struck a railway station platform in Dnipro, Ukraine, on 29 October, killing 13 people and injuring at least five others, according to Ukrainian officials. Regional military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha first described the target as transport infrastructure before later confirming the death toll. Dnipro's mayor, Borys Filatov, said a drone hit a civilian electric train, while state railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said the platform was crowded and an air-raid alert had been issued beforehand.

The train bound for Zaporizhzhia, number 866, was stationed nearby at the time. Separately, a 15-year-old girl was reported injured in a Russian strike on Pavlohrad in the same oblast.

actors.why: Thirteen civilians killed and several injured in a strike on a rail station
Accused by Ukrainian officials of launching the drone strike on civilians

impact_points: Ukraine faces heavy civilian losses and disruption to its rail network after a strike on a busy Dnipro platform.
Russia is accused of targeting a civilian train station, a claim that raises further international scrutiny of its attacks on Ukrainian cities.

auto-4dfc5dac5be9.headline: US war on Iran costs taxpayers at least $47.1bn, Pentagon tells Congress
auto-4dfc5dac5be9.summary: The Pentagon has informed US lawmakers that its military campaign against Iran had cost taxpayers at least $47.1 billion as of October 16. Figures shared with the New York Times include roughly $29 billion to replace used munitions, with the Air Force, Navy and Army accounting for large shares of spending. The estimate excludes fuel and repairs to damaged bases. The disclosure comes days before the November 3 US midterm elections, as the war's rising costs and fuel price impacts fuel political criticism.

actors.why: Bears mounting war costs and energy price pressure, with midterm political fallout
Target of the campaign and has closed the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting global supplies
Named as a co-participant in the US-Israel war on Iran

impact_points: The United States faces rising military and fiscal costs, with estimates climbing steadily as the war continues.
American households and farmers face higher diesel and energy prices after Iran's disruption of the Strait of Hormuz.

auto-6cb5951f5c54.headline: US weighs easing sanctions on Russia's state investment fund amid talks
auto-6cb5951f5c54.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly considering lifting US sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund, a state-backed vehicle Moscow uses to extend its global influence. Russian officials have pushed for relief as part of wider negotiations that include the fund's role in supplying diesel to the United States. A US official linked the possible move to improving relations and ending the war in Ukraine, and praised the fund's head, Kirill Dmitriev, as a helpful envoy. The Treasury Department is reviewing the request under its normal process, which requires the fund to show the original reasons for sanctions no longer apply. Critics, including some Republicans, argue the approach rewards Moscow without pressing it to end the war.

actors.why: Possible sanctions relief would restore the fund's Western financial access and influence
Reversing sanctions would depart from years of economic pressure and draw political criticism
Easing pressure on Moscow could prolong the war Ukraine is fighting

impact_points: Russia would gain access to Western finance and economic leverage if the sanctions were lifted.
Ukraine and critics of the approach see the move as weakening economic pressure on Moscow over the war.

auto-27ad97d9743a.headline: UN assembly overwhelmingly backs ending US economic restrictions on Cuba
auto-27ad97d9743a.summary: The UN General Assembly passed a resolution calling for an end to the long-standing US embargo on Cuba, with 130 votes in favour, 17 against and 25 abstentions. The text also urges countries to repeal laws such as the 1996 Helms-Burton Act, which it says has extraterritorial effects that undermine other states' sovereignty. It marks the 34th consecutive year the assembly has taken up the matter. Cuban leaders welcomed the result as a victory, while Havana's official figures put the economic cost of the embargo at nearly $179 billion.

actors.why: Gains international backing; embargo costs estimated near $179 billion by Havana
Sanctions policy criticised by most assembly members in the vote

impact_points: Cuba gains diplomatic backing as the vote shows broad international opposition to the US embargo.
The United States faces renewed isolation over its sanctions policy, though the resolution itself is not binding on Washington.

auto-5b7f5a8c3eb9.headline: Ethiopia takes delivery of Russian fighter jets and air defence systems
auto-5b7f5a8c3eb9.summary:
Ethiopia has received a batch of fighter aircraft and air defence equipment from Russia, according to the report. The deliveries come as fighting intensifies in the northern Tigray region, which borders Eritrea. The article's text is partial, so further details on the number of aircraft, timing and contract terms could not be confirmed from the portion available.

The arrival of the weapons is significant because it strengthens Ethiopia's air power during an active internal conflict on its northern frontier. It also points to deepening military ties between Addis Ababa and Moscow.

actors.why: Receives Russian jets and air defence amid Tigray fighting, boosting military capacity
Supplies fighter jets and air defence systems, expanding its arms ties in Africa
Neighbour facing a better-armed Ethiopian air force near the Tigray border

impact_points: Ethiopia gains stronger air power and air defence while fighting continues in Tigray.
Eritrea and Tigray's armed groups face a more capable Ethiopian air force near their borders.

auto-561fe0a1c8cf.headline: Houthi strike on Aden airport injures civilians as Yemen fighting intensifies
auto-561fe0a1c8cf.summary: Yemeni government forces said Houthi fighters struck Aden airport, the main gateway to southern Yemen, after the group warned people to leave the site. The attack injured civilians and damaged property, and air traffic was halted, officials said. Residents also reported blasts elsewhere in the city, and the UN and aid groups said their staff were safe. The Houthis said the warning was prompted by a Saudi military cargo plane they claimed was carrying weapons; Saudi authorities did not comment. The strike comes amid escalating fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition, which has shattered a 2022 truce.

actors.why: Aden airport struck, civilians injured and key aid route disrupted
Houthi attacks escalate and coalition strikes intensify against Houthi positions
Houthi front opens in wider conflict involving Iran, seen as aligned gain

impact_points: Yemen's government and its humanitarian operations face disruption, as Aden airport is a key route for aid and medical supplies.
Saudi Arabia faces a renewed front with the Houthis, which Riyadh is responding to with stepped-up strikes against Houthi positions.

auto-ae2fff49913a.headline: Moscow hosts African leaders at summit aimed at widening Russian reach
auto-ae2fff49913a.summary: Over 20 African leaders have gathered in Moscow for a two-day Russia-Africa summit, the third of its kind since 2019. Delegations from 48 African countries are attending, including 22 heads of state, and Vladimir Putin plans bilateral meetings with most of them. The event comes as Russia faces heavy sanctions over its war in Ukraine, while some African governments seek Russian security help. Discussions are expected to center on economic cooperation, including agricultural exports, localized medicine production and digital technology, with a final declaration due Thursday. Analysts quoted in the report note that Russia's ties with Africa remain largely military and security-focused, and that the Ukraine war may limit Moscow's ability to fund its ambitions.

actors.why: Hosts summit to expand influence despite sanctions and budget strain
Named as a target of Russian neocolonialism narrative by Moscow
Ukraine war weighs on Russia's ability to fund African ambitions

impact_points: Russia is seeking to expand its influence across Africa and present itself as a leader of the Global South.
African governments relying on Russian security help and grain or fertiliser supplies may face shifting ties as Moscow's budget tightens.

auto-8a9b24ef4517.headline: Vance reportedly writes to Iran's security chief as Trump warns of possible strikes
auto-8a9b24ef4517.summary: US Vice President JD Vance has reportedly sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, who leads Iran's Supreme National Security Council, aiming to revive stalled peace talks. US media say Iran received the letter positively, and the Qatari mediators passed it on. According to officials cited by the media, the letter calls for direct talks with Iran's nuclear programme on the agenda from the start, possibly in Qatar or Turkiye. The outreach comes as Trump reportedly warned Gulf allies to prepare for a brief, intense military campaign after next week's US midterm elections. Iran has not publicly commented, and Rezaei is expected to respond on Thursday.

actors.why: Faces possible renewed US strikes but has an opening for talks
Vance seeks talks while Trump threatens a short intense campaign
Qatari mediators passed the letter and may host talks
Named as a possible venue for negotiations
Gulf ally reportedly warned to prepare for possible US military action

impact_points: Iran faces a choice between renewed US strikes and a negotiating track led by Vance.
Gulf states, including Qatar, are affected as mediators and potential venues, and as possible targets of renewed conflict.

auto-42416c7b938a.headline: NATO allies worry Patriot interceptors for Ukraine may be held until after US elections
auto-42416c7b938a.summary: NATO allies reportedly expect Ukraine may not receive sought-after US Patriot interceptor missiles before the US midterm elections. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Kyiv is still awaiting approval from US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, while NATO sources describe the timing as unpredictable. Sources link the delay to US pressure on Ukraine, including demands to halt strikes on Russian diesel refineries, amid high energy prices after the Iran conflict. Russia has reportedly fired more than 100 ballistic missiles at Kyiv region in two weeks, far outpacing estimated US monthly interceptor output.

actors.why: Air defence shortfall leaves Kyiv exposed to repeated Russian ballistic missile attacks
Interceptor stocks strained by Iran war and used as leverage over Kyiv
Intensified missile campaign against Ukraine benefits from delayed air defence supplies
Reportedly holds PAC-2 stockpiles that NATO wants transferred but has not released
Reportedly holds PAC-2 stockpiles that NATO wants transferred but has not released

impact_points: Ukraine faces a shortage of air defence interceptors as Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv continue.
Greece and Spain hold PAC-2 Patriot systems that NATO has asked them to hand over, and they have not agreed.

auto-2faaed9e93b3.headline: Truce in Oleshky allows aid and evacuation, US says Melania Trump helped secure it
auto-2faaed9e93b3.summary: Fighting in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has paused under a truce that the White House credits to US First Lady Melania Trump. The arrangement is intended to let aid reach the city and allow civilians to be evacuated on Friday. Some residents told the BBC they doubted the ceasefire, since the evacuation routes could run through Crimea and Russia. The report also refers to a separate attack on Ukrainian commuters attributed to Moscow's forces.

actors.why: Residents gain possible aid and evacuation, though the truce is fragile.
Moscow's forces are blamed for strikes on commuters during the truce period.
Washington gains diplomatic credit for securing the truce via the First Lady.

impact_points: Ukraine's civilians in Oleshky stand to gain aid and a possible evacuation, though some residents remain sceptical of the route.
Russia faces scrutiny over the truce and the attack on commuters, while the US presents itself as a broker in the pause.

auto-924e3f7e189f.headline: Saudi-led coalition downs Houthi missile aimed at Eastern Province
auto-924e3f7e189f.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's government said it destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province early Thursday. Saudi civil defence had issued warnings for both Najran and the Eastern Province before saying the threat had passed. Separately, the article reports that Houthi attacks on villages and residential areas in Lahj and Taiz have forced hundreds of families to flee, with government sources saying the attacks use missiles, drones and mortars after the group made little ground progress.

Aid agencies warned that conditions for displaced people are worsening, with about 5.2 million internally displaced and 2.2 million children under five acutely malnourished. The article notes 22.3 million Yemenis need aid.

actors.why: Targeted by a Houthi ballistic missile; civil defence issued threat warnings
Houthi attacks displace families and deepen humanitarian crisis

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces a direct missile threat to its Eastern Province and Najran, though the coalition says it intercepted the projectile.
Yemeni civilians in Lahj and Taiz face displacement and shrinking access to aid as attacks on residential areas intensify.

auto-c13b0a9bba9b.headline: Netanyahu narrowly leads Eisenkot as Israel's coalition talks look difficult
auto-c13b0a9bba9b.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu holds a slight lead over opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot in the Knesset election count, with about 93 percent of votes tallied. Netanyahu's right-wing religious bloc is projected at 53 of 120 seats, while Eisenkot's bloc is at 48. Israeli Arab parties rose to around 19 seats, making them potential kingmakers, though neither leader appears able to form a majority easily. President Isaac Herzog will decide who gets the first chance to build a coalition, and a new vote could follow if talks fail. Israeli markets fell sharply on the uncertainty.

actors.why: Coalition deadlock and market losses create instability at home
Netanyahu hints at renewed strikes, with Trump backing the threat
Trump endorsed Netanyahu and may join renewed strikes on Iran

impact_points: Israel faces weeks of uncertainty over forming a government, with a possible repeat election looming.
Israeli Arab parties hold leverage in negotiations, while Iran faces renewed threats of strikes from Netanyahu and Trump.

auto-919063f3ae3e.headline: Opinion piece argues US-Israel war on Iran will resume without a change of course
auto-919063f3ae3e.summary: An opinion column in Al Jazeera contends that the conflict Israel and the United States began against Iran on February 28 is only paused, not over. The author argues both governments pursue aims that rule out peace: Israel seeking regional military dominance and the US preserving its global position. The piece points to signs of renewed fighting, including reported planning for strikes on Iranian petrochemical and nuclear sites, a US naval blockade of Iranian ports now over 100 days old, and Israel's upcoming October 27 election. It also notes Iran's warnings of retaliation and an energy crisis, and says Gulf states now face heightened risk from hosting US bases.

actors.why: Faces renewed strikes, blockade and threats to its territory and shipping
Planning renewed strikes; the column frames its leadership as pursuing dominance
Blockade and war planning continue; column criticises its strategy as reckless
Gulf host states described as exposed to Iranian retaliation and energy disruption

impact_points: Iran faces renewed strikes and blockade pressure, and has threatened retaliation against regional bases and shipping.
Gulf states hosting US bases are described as exposed to attacks and an energy crisis if fighting resumes.

auto-3cf5733f3fe8.headline: QatarEnergy turns to US and other LNG supplies to hedge Hormuz risks
auto-3cf5733f3fe8.summary: QatarEnergy, the state energy company of Qatar, has bought liquefied natural gas from the United States and other suppliers. The purchases are intended to protect its supply against future disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. The move comes as the strait remains affected by the wider conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran. The report is based on an exclusive account of the company's contracts, and the reporting frames the deals as a hedge rather than a response to a single incident.

actors.why: Diversifying supply to hedge against Hormuz disruption, reducing its exposure
Gains a major new LNG buyer through the purchases from American suppliers
Regional tensions and the Hormuz risk are linked to the wider conflict with Iran

impact_points: Qatar's LNG exports depend on the Strait of Hormuz, so its state energy firm is diversifying supply to reduce that exposure.
US LNG producers gain a major new buyer, as QatarEnergy becomes a significant purchaser of American gas.

auto-13e1ab2ed680.headline: Hegseth removes Pentagon's top strategy officer as Iran strike options are considered
auto-13e1ab2ed680.summary:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has dismissed Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia from his role running strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff, according to a defence official who spoke on condition of anonymity. The official said no reason was given and there is no immediate successor. Sylvia is the second holder of the post to leave under Hegseth, following Lieutenant General Joseph McGee, who was forced to retire last October. The removal came as President Donald Trump was reportedly weighing renewed strikes on Iran in a conflict that has run for eight months.

The dismissal was first reported by The Atlantic.

actors.why: Top military planning post left vacant amid leadership turnover and weighed Iran strikes
Faces possible renewed US strikes during an eight-month conflict

impact_points: The United States military's planning leadership is left without a head, with no immediate replacement named for the Joint Chiefs post.
Iran faces the prospect of renewed American strikes at a time when the Pentagon's strategy office is in flux.

auto-1ec7066bc8d4.headline: Vance reportedly reaches out to Iran's security chief to revive talks
auto-1ec7066bc8d4.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, who heads Iran's Supreme National Security Council, in an effort to restart peace talks. The move was described by one source as directed by President Donald Trump. The letter and later contacts reportedly focused on a broad framework for negotiations rather than specific proposals. The report also says Washington told several Gulf states to prepare for a possible short, intense military campaign against Iran after the November 3 US midterm elections, though Trump has reportedly not made a final decision.

actors.why: Faces possible renewed strikes and talks offer, amid a blockade and economic squeeze
Seeks renewed negotiations while preparing options for possible military action
Part of the US-Israeli campaign against Iran that could resume
Told to prepare for possible Iran campaign and hit by energy disruption and oil spill risk

impact_points: Iran faces renewed pressure as talks are sought while a possible US-Israeli strike looms over it.
Gulf countries are being asked to prepare for possible military action, and global energy supplies remain disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

auto-054608bfd9c5.headline: Russian lower house advances record defence budget funded by new taxes
auto-054608bfd9c5.summary: Russia's State Duma gave first-reading approval to a three-year federal budget that sets aside a record sum for defence, with security spending making up 44% of government outlays. To pay for it, the plan trims funding for economic support, healthcare, social support and housing, and raises revenue through a 22% VAT on cross-border online retail, higher taxes on certain passive income and dividends, and a levy on excess profits in mining and metallurgy. The bill passed 372 to zero with 51 abstentions and now moves to a second reading, then the Federation Council, before needing President Vladimir Putin's signature.

actors.why: Record defence spending funded by cuts to civilian programmes and new taxes
Russia's budget expands military spending tied to the war in Ukraine

impact_points: Russia's citizens face cuts to healthcare, social support and housing funding as military spending rises.
Businesses and investors in Russia face new taxes on online imports, dividends, passive income and mining profits.

auto-0470add51a00.headline: US and Japan plan joint Japanese plant for advanced air-to-air missiles
auto-0470add51a00.summary: Japan and the United States have agreed to set up a facility in Japan to jointly produce advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles, Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said on October 28, 2026, at a news conference in Cebu, Philippines. The missiles, part of a joint effort called Operation Supercharge, are described by Koizumi as essential for the F-35 fighter jet, though he gave no further details. He made the announcement after meeting US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of a regional defence meeting, where both officials stressed deterrence without naming China.

actors.why: Gains joint missile production facility and stronger alliance deterrence with the US
Deepens missile co-production and reaffirms regional deterrence commitments
Receives renewed US assurances of defence support amid South China Sea tensions
Faces a strengthened US-Japan alliance and deterrence posture, though not named

impact_points: Japan gains a domestic production base for key F-35-linked missiles, strengthening its defence capabilities and alliance ties.
China and regional states in the South China Sea face a firmer US deterrence posture, with Washington pledging to defend the Philippines.

auto-d04492f5c82c.headline: US cost-of-living strain and a split economy weigh on midterm politics
auto-d04492f5c82c.summary: A France 24 segment examines how rising food and energy prices are shaping voter concerns ahead of the November 2026 US midterm elections. Greg Ip, chief economics commentator at The Wall Street Journal, argues that the outcome of the midterms would do little to ease the cost-of-living problem, since presidential powers over matters such as the war in Iran and tariffs are separate from Congress. He describes a gap between strong GDP figures, which mainly benefit companies and wealthier households tied to the AI boom, and ordinary households whose incomes lag behind. The report also covers local opposition to AI data centres in Republican-leaning states such as Texas, which Ip sees as a proxy for wider anxiety about AI.

actors.why: Voters face cost-of-living strain and a divided economy ahead of midterms
Mentioned only as the subject of the US-linked war, affected indirectly

impact_points: American voters, especially median households, face strained incomes and high food and energy costs.
Congress and the Trump administration face pressure over inflation, tariffs and the AI economy's uneven gains.

auto-bb0bdeae3126.headline: Syrians angered by government response to deadly Jordanian strikes in Daraa
auto-bb0bdeae3126.summary: Jordan's military said its air force struck sites in Syria's southern Daraa province, targeting groups it linked to a church shooting in southern Jordan that killed nine people. The Islamic State group later claimed the shooting. Jordanian officials said more than 20 IS members and a weapons depot were hit, while acknowledging civilian deaths. Damascus rejected Amman's claim that the strikes were coordinated with it, condemned them as a sovereignty violation and summoned Jordan's ambassador. A joint statement by the Syrian and Jordanian foreign ministers, which set up a security committee, has drawn anger from many Syrians who see it as accepting Jordan's account.

actors.why: Civilians killed in its territory and government criticised for weak response
Strikes on Syrian soil with civilian toll, though framed as counterterrorism
Commentators warn the episode could be used to justify wider Israeli occupation in Syria

Jordan faces scrutiny over its strikes and civilian casualties, though its officials frame them as counterterrorism.

auto-3361da11fba4.headline: Settlers raid West Bank villages and assault activists and a journalist
auto-3361da11fba4.summary: Armed Israeli settlers reportedly entered the Palestinian community of Al-Shuneh in the Jordan Valley before dawn, surrounding homes and urging residents to leave, according to the UK charity Medical Aid for Palestinians. The group said settlers also took a water tank and appear to be building an outpost on a nearby hill, affecting about 80 families. In Masafer Yatta, activist Adele Shoko said settlers beat her, two colleagues and a US journalist, and that Israeli forces detained the journalist. These accounts come from the sources named and could not be independently verified.

auto-df8e6a00fbc4.headline: Abbas hopes new Israeli government reopens peace talks
auto-df8e6a00fbc4.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas said on Thursday, at a news conference in Cyprus, that he hoped a newly formed Israeli government would open the way to renewed serious political dialogue and progress toward peace. His remarks were relayed by the Palestinian official news agency Wafa and reported by AFP. The statement signals Ramallah's wish for talks to resume once Israel's new administration is in place, though it does not describe any specific proposal or scheduled meeting. The article also includes a separate feature on how children in Gaza face years of lost schooling after nearly three years of war.

auto-e42483718cbd.headline: Russia plans longer diesel export ban and quotas to meet US deal, sources say
auto-e42483718cbd.summary: Russia intends to extend its ban on diesel exports and rely on quotas to honour an arrangement with the United States, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke to Reuters. The sources indicate the measures are being shaped around the commitments Moscow has made to Washington on fuel supply. The report does not give a firm timetable for the extension or the size of the quotas. Details could not be independently confirmed by the wire service at the time of publication.

Would receive diesel volumes under the agreed arrangement with Moscow

impact_points: Russia's domestic fuel market would stay tightly controlled, with exports limited by government-set quotas rather than open sales.
The United States stands to receive supplies under the agreement, while buyers relying on Russian diesel may face restricted availability.

auto-b4bf60d907cd.headline: Most Ukrainians back strikes on Russian refineries even without US aid
auto-b4bf60d907cd.summary:
A Kyiv International Institute of Sociology poll of 828 adults in government-controlled Ukraine, conducted 16 to 25 October, found 80% favour continuing strikes on Russian oil refineries even if Washington halts or limits its aid. Only 11% said such strikes should stop, and 8% were undecided. The survey also found 63% of respondents were ready to endure the war for as long as necessary.

The poll was conducted by telephone, and the institute noted that wartime conditions can introduce a systematic deviation beyond the stated margin of error.

actors.why: Public backing for refinery strikes signals sustained resolve despite aid uncertainty
Strong Ukrainian public support suggests refinery strikes will likely continue
Poll suggests Ukraine may keep striking even if American aid is cut

Russia faces continued pressure on its oil refining capacity if Ukrainian strikes persist, according to the poll's implied public mood.

auto-f4924af22287.headline: Fighting pauses in occupied Oleshky under truce for aid and evacuation
auto-f4924af22287.summary: Fighting in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has stopped under a truce that the White House credits to US First Lady Melania Trump. The arrangement is intended to let aid reach the city and allow civilians to be evacuated on Friday. Residents told the BBC they were uneasy about the pause, since the proposed evacuation routes could lead through Crimea and Russia.

White House claims credit for brokering the truce, a diplomatic gain.

auto-46cd1f474fe4.headline: UN assembly again backs ending US economic embargo on Cuba
auto-46cd1f474fe4.summary: The UN General Assembly passed a resolution calling for an end to the US economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba, with 130 countries in favour and 17 against, including the United States and Israel. Another 25 abstained, among them Germany and Italy, which had voted in favour in earlier years. Cuba's foreign minister welcomed the outcome, saying Washington was isolated. US Ambassador Mike Waltz said more countries had shifted their stance and expected the trend to continue. The vote followed a clash between US and Cuban diplomats, and the US said a Cuban UN mission official would be expelled.

auto-9d44b7aa8f1f.headline: Canada and EU hold Montreal summit on deeper ties and associate status
auto-9d44b7aa8f1f.summary: Canada and the European Union are meeting in Montreal for a two-day summit aimed at drawing the two sides closer together. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described a possible "associate membership" for Canada, a status that does not yet exist, as a partnership nearly as close as full membership, covering policy alignment and joint research. Some member states, including Germany, have questioned the term, and a draft statement reportedly dropped it in favour of softer wording about an "ever closer association". Officials expect deals on defence, critical minerals, research and trade, while EU officials have played down any major announcement. US President Donald Trump has dismissed the idea as "laughable".

impact_points: Canada gains closer access to EU programmes and markets, without a membership fee, as it diversifies away from the US.

auto-1c9081040159.headline: Serbian police kill knife-wielding attacker outside Israeli embassy in Belgrade
auto-1c9081040159.summary:
Serbian police shot dead a young man outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade early Wednesday after officials described the incident as a terrorist attack. Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said the assailant charged an officer with two knives while shouting a religious phrase. The officer suffered a minor facial wound and is reported to be recovering without hospital treatment.

The suspect, a minor and Serbian citizen previously under security monitoring, was reportedly linked to Islamic State. Serbia raised its terrorism threat level to red alert. Israel's foreign ministry said no embassy staff were hurt, and the mission was closed at the time. It is the second attack on the embassy in under three years.

actors.why: Attack on capital's embassy forces red alert and heavier security checks
Its embassy in Belgrade was attacked again, though no staff were hurt

impact_points: Serbia faces heightened security demands and a raised terrorism alert after the attack on its capital.
Israel's embassy in Belgrade is again targeted, raising concerns about the safety of its diplomatic staff.

auto-e3e051f10f2a.headline: Ukraine's navy claims strike on Russian airfield destroys two Su-34 bombers
auto-e3e051f10f2a.summary: Ukraine's navy says it struck the Marinovka airfield in Russia's Volgograd Oblast on Thursday 29 October, using a Long Neptune missile. According to the navy, the strike destroyed two Su-34 fighter-bombers at the 11th Composite Aviation Regiment in Oktyabrsky. The navy describes the Su-34 as a key Russian tactical aircraft used to drop guided bombs on Ukrainian cities and front-line positions. These claims come from the Ukrainian side and could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Two Su-34 bombers reportedly destroyed at a Volgograd Oblast airbase
Claimed long-range strike demonstrates missile reach against Russian airfields

impact_points: Russia loses two Su-34 aircraft, reducing its tactical bombing capacity used against Ukrainian front lines and cities.
Ukraine gains a reported success deep inside Russian territory, signalling reach of its long-range missile systems.

auto-37b972d5887a.headline: Pentagon puts Iran war cost at $47.1bn before US midterms
auto-37b972d5887a.summary: The Pentagon has told US lawmakers that the war with Iran has cost American taxpayers at least $47.1 billion as of mid-October. The estimate includes about $29 billion to replace used munitions and spending by the Air Force, Navy and Army. It excludes repairs to damaged Middle East bases and fuel costs. Officials say 18 service members have been publicly acknowledged killed, though some reports put the toll higher. Critics, including Democratic senators, accuse the administration of hiding the true cost ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

Targeted by the war and has closed the Strait of Hormuz
Partner in the US-Israel war on Iran, sharing its costs and risks

impact_points: The United States faces mounting military and budget costs, with the figure likely a running total rather than the final cost.
Iran and the wider Gulf region face ongoing disruption, including the closure of the Strait of Hormuz affecting global energy supplies.

auto-131048f98cac.headline: US removes army general from Joint Chiefs planning post amid Iran tensions
auto-131048f98cac.summary: The United States has dismissed Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, who led strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff, according to a report by The Atlantic on Wednesday. The removal came this week and is described as the latest high-profile military departure since Donald Trump returned to office a year ago. The move coincides with reports that Trump may be preparing to resume large-scale strikes against Iran.

auto-781a4d9ed9ba.headline: Former Biden officials urge 2028 candidates to bar Gaza war enablers
auto-781a4d9ed9ba.summary:
A group of twelve former officials from the Biden administration has issued a letter asking every 2028 US presidential hopeful not to recruit former staff who helped Israel's conduct in Gaza. Most signatories served at the State Department, intelligence agencies or the military, and include both Arab and Jewish Americans. The letter says the officials concealed facts, misled the public and suppressed dissent, and calls for accountability. It cites more than 250,000 Palestinians killed or injured since the October 2023 war began, and urges candidates to acknowledge US complicity.

The letter follows admissions by several ex-officials that Washington should have acted sooner to halt the Israeli campaign. The article also notes that former spokesperson Matthew Miller and ex-adviser Jake Sullivan have voiced criticism, and that Kamala Harris recently said the administration fell short on human rights.

auto-cf449c2db37a.headline: Greek ship sunk by drone off Bulgaria prompts call for maritime truce
auto-cf449c2db37a.summary:
A Greek container ship was sunk by a drone attack off the Bulgarian coast, the latest in a string of strikes on vessels in the western Black Sea this month. Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis used a UN Security Council debate on maritime security to call for a global maritime truce, saying attacks on civilian commercial shipping are unacceptable.

Mitsotakis also argued that disruption to navigation raises shipping and insurance costs that ultimately reach consumers. He criticised a Turkey-Libya maritime accord, which Greece, Cyprus and three Arab states have condemned, saying no bilateral deal can override the international law of the sea.

auto-c0aa44734394.headline: China promotes anti-corruption military chief Zhang Shengmin to Politburo
auto-c0aa44734394.summary: China has elevated General Zhang Shengmin to the Politburo, the Communist Party's top decision-making body. Zhang, a vice-chair of the Central Military Commission, led the military's anti-corruption work from 2018 until July of this year and has been the main enforcer of the campaign against graft in the People's Liberation Army. That campaign has removed many senior military officers, leaving the seven-member Commission with only two members: President Xi Jinping and Zhang himself. The move comes alongside an official communique describing next year's 21st party congress as taking place at a critical stage on China's path toward its second centenary goal.

actors.why: Reinforces party discipline and consolidates leadership ahead of the 2027 congress

impact_points: China's military leadership is being reshaped, with a key anti-corruption figure gaining a seat at the top of party power.

auto-c0bff78b7151.summary: An opinion piece says the February 28 US-Israeli war on Iran is paused rather than over, and that both governments are set to resume fighting. The author argues Israel's leadership is driven by a goal of regional military dominance tied to the Palestinians, while Washington is motivated by preserving its global standing and long-running hostility toward Iran. The piece cites a planned renewed campaign reportedly aimed at Iranian petrochemical and nuclear sites, the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, and Israel's October 27 election. It also warns that Gulf states hosting US bases have become targets.

auto-7e982712e422.headline: El Salvador sends over 2,000 troops to Haiti after four soldiers vanish
auto-7e982712e422.summary: El Salvador has deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti to recover four nationals who disappeared there nearly two weeks ago. President Nayib Bukele informed Haiti's prime minister of the deployment, and the foreign ministry said the troops would also support efforts against gangs. The four men were air force technicians serving with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force, and they were ambushed in Croix-des-Bouquets while returning to base. No group has claimed the attack. auto-725450b2e597.headline: Iraqi court jails two politicians and orders repayments in oil refinery graft case
auto-725450b2e597.summary: An Iraqi court has sentenced two senior Sunni politicians to prison over profits from contracts linked to the North and South Refineries companies. Muthanna al-Samarrai, who leads Iraq's second-largest Sunni political alliance, received six years and must repay 30 billion Iraqi dinars. Lawmaker Ziad al-Janabi, a former chair of parliament's Integrity Committee, got five years and an order to return 4 billion dinars. The ruling was announced by the judiciary as part of an anti-corruption drive begun under Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, though the campaign has reportedly lost momentum. The verdicts can be appealed within 30 days.

auto-5444aea55585.headline: Healey unveils £100 energy payments as UK budget absorbs Middle East shock
auto-5444aea55585.summary:
Chancellor John Healey presented Britain's first budget under Labour, pointing to global economic pressures and the Middle East conflict as reasons the outlook has worsened. The centrepiece is a £100 payment for around 20 million households in council tax bands A to D, costing £2.6bn, with matching funds for Scotland and Wales, whose governments can decide whether to pass it on. The package is paid for by a higher bank surcharge and a two-point income tax rise affecting landlords and savers.

Healey said higher inflation linked to the Iran war would add about £14bn to interest costs, and the Office for Budget Responsibility cut next year's growth forecast to 1%. He still pledged to meet the fiscal rule on balancing current spending by 2029-30, though with reduced headroom of £15bn.

Mentioned only as a general economic backdrop; no direct link in the text

auto-fb9c639de364.headline: Houthi-run health ministry reports 12 dead in Taiz strike, blames Saudi Arabia

auto-28161601b2ca.headline: Quiet returns to Kherson as a short truce allows aid into occupied Oleshky

auto-ae61f5d3e102.headline: Israeli raids and settler attacks injure and detain Palestinians across the West Bank
auto-ae61f5d3e102.summary: Israeli forces and settlers carried out raids, assaults, arrests and home demolitions across the occupied West Bank, according to Palestinian and aid sources. In the Qalandiya refugee camp near East Jerusalem, two children were wounded during a raid, the Palestine Red Crescent Society said. Israeli military operations in the Hebron governorate, now in their seventh day after two Israeli soldiers were killed in a gun attack, have forced or besieged hundreds of families and disrupted schooling for many students. The UN humanitarian office OCHA called for an end to further displacement and demolitions.

actors.why: Families displaced, children wounded, detentions and demolitions across the West Bank

auto-f10151bd1c0d.headline: Russia courts African leaders at Moscow summit, pitching itself as an alternative partner
auto-f10151bd1c0d.summary: President Vladimir Putin hosted African leaders at the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow. He told them Russia makes a better partner than Western countries, and said Russian firms work in Africa on equal terms, while accusing the West of still chasing the continent's resources. The article notes some African states have turned to Russia for security help, that trade and economic ties are expanding, and that Moscow promotes a "multipolar world" while seeking Global South backing against Western pressure over its war in Ukraine. A panel of analysts was brought in to assess what both sides gain from the gathering.

Accused by Putin of exploiting African resources; faces competition for African influence

Russia gains diplomatic support from the Global South while seeking to ease Western pressure over Ukraine.

auto-a645acc10f57.headline: Lagarde to leave ECB early, citing freedom to speak on wider issues
auto-a645acc10f57.summary: Christine Lagarde, president of the European Central Bank, plans to step down several months ahead of schedule. She said the move would give her more room to take part in discussions beyond monetary policy. The announcement has prompted speculation about her next move, given that France, her home country, is set to hold a presidential election. Her departure also opens a contest to choose her successor at a time when Europe faces challenging public finances.

actors.why: Lagarde's exit fuels speculation about a French political role before its presidential vote
Leadership change at the ECB comes as the bloc faces a turbulent fiscal outlook

impact_points: The European Central Bank must now find a new leader to guide eurozone monetary policy during a difficult period.
France and the wider eurozone face speculation over Lagarde's future role, which could shape the political landscape ahead of the French election.

auto-6d299a19992d.headline: Kherson quiet as six-day truce brings humanitarian aid to Oleshky
auto-6d299a19992d.summary: A six-day ceasefire has brought a rare lull in fighting to Kherson, the Ukrainian-held city on the Dnipro's west bank. Ukraine and Russia are linked by the truce, which tests whether humanitarian pauses can hold in the war.

auto-886e79f121a5.headline: Israeli strikes kill two in Gaza as health officials press for Rafah reopening
auto-886e79f121a5.summary:
Israeli drone and artillery attacks continued across Gaza on Thursday, with at least two Palestinians killed in a strike on a car in the Maghazi camp in central Gaza. Other strikes hit northern areas and eastern Gaza City, and four aid-monitoring workers were reported killed near Rafah. Gaza's Health Ministry reported six deaths and 38 injuries over the previous day.

The ministry urged that the Rafah crossing with Egypt be reopened so that 21,468 patients and wounded people needing treatment abroad, including 6,430 priority cases, can leave. It blamed border closures and delays for worsening conditions, and said 3,056 people have been evacuated since February.

Israeli forces conduct the strikes and control the crossings that limit evacuations
Rafah crossing with Egypt is central to the evacuation pleas and would share the burden of reopening

auto-e8ab14dbd616.headline: Senior Chinese general elevated to the ruling party's top decision-making body
auto-e8ab14dbd616.summary: A senior Chinese military official has been named to the Politburo, the inner circle that steers the Communist Party's policy. Rising military influence in Beijing may heighten Washington's strategic concerns
Elevated Chinese military leadership could raise pressure over Taiwan policy

auto-cbd6ce005e67.headline: Russian drone strike on Dnipro rail platform kills at least 14
auto-cbd6ce005e67.summary: A jet-powered drone struck a crowded platform at the main railway station in Dnipro, central Ukraine, killing at least 14 people and wounding 14 more, including an 11-year-old boy, according to regional officials. Ukraine's state railway operator said a passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was at the platform when the strike hit. Russia's military had not publicly commented. Elsewhere, Ukrainian officials reported two teenage girls killed in a missile attack on Chernihiv and three deaths in a drone strike on Kremenchuk.

Zelensky criticises a recent deal easing sanctions allowing Russian diesel imports
Asked by Kyiv to join further sanctions on Russia

Russia is criticised over strikes on civilians, while Ukrainian President Zelensky urges fresh US, European and G7 sanctions against Moscow.

auto-84edbb4f4c19.summary: North Korea staged a weapons demonstration featuring suicide attack drones, armed multipurpose drones, cruise missiles and 600mm rocket launchers, according to state media KCNA. The show came a day after South Korea's military reported around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles fired from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea, about 250 kilometres. auto-cc5ffedde57b.summary: El Salvador has deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti to recover four of its nationals who went missing almost two weeks ago. The men were technicians serving with a UN-backed anti-gang force, the Gang Suppression Force, and were ambushed while driving an armoured vehicle in Croix-des-Bouquets, an area held by armed groups. No gang has claimed the attack. President Nayib Bukele informed Haiti's prime minister of the deployment, which his foreign ministry said would also support efforts against gangs. Haiti earlier handed over four bodies that it said belonged to the missing men, but Bukele disputed the identification.

auto-14067912993c.summary: US Central Command has rejected Iranian media reports that commercial ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz have struck sea mines, calling the claims false. auto-ebdf0d44ce52.headline: Israel's election tightens as Netanyahu and Eisenkot vie for a governing majority
auto-ebdf0d44ce52.summary:
Partial counts from Israel's national election show a close contest between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc and the alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot, with neither clearly reaching the 61 seats needed in the 120-seat Knesset. With over 84 percent of votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc was on track for 54 seats, Eisenkot's for 49, and Arab parties for 17. Turnout reached 77.7 percent, the highest since 1999.

auto-4771af0b01a3.summary: A trade dispute between the United States and Canada is reportedly damaging Kentucky's bourbon industry, which brings in billions of dollars a year in a state that has long leaned Republican. auto-e0187192e0e3.summary: Australia's federal antisemitism envoy, Jillian Segal, has released an updated plan recommending that an external, independent ombudsman oversee coverage of the Gaza war by the ABC and SBS. auto-92a0252dfe37.headline: Seven Russian diesel tankers head for US amid legal dispute over deal

auto-82761fdfa67f.summary:
Russia's Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said European countries will not take part in the next round of Ukraine, US and Russia talks planned for Abu Dhabi, citing a recent Putin call with the Finnish and Norwegian leaders. Finnish President Alexander Stubb later said Europe would be involved, creating conflicting accounts. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, speaking in the Netherlands, said trilateral talks would run November 6 to 10 and that Kyiv wants Europe included.

In The Hague, the Dutch government pledged new military and energy aid to Ukraine, and the UK announced a further 10 billion pounds in support, including 500 million pounds for air defences this winter.

actors.why: Excludes Europe from talks, but faces growing Western military support for Ukraine
Gains major new British and Dutch military and energy aid
Hosts trilateral talks with Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi
Pledges 1.2 billion euros over three years plus extra military funding
Announces 10 billion pound package, including 500 million for air defences
Stubb publicly contradicts Kremlin on European role in talks

impact_points: Ukraine is pressing for European involvement in talks, seeking unity and stronger pressure on Russia.
Russia faces a stronger European aid push, with new Dutch and British packages aimed at its air defence and energy targets.

auto-974200daab33.headline: Washington reportedly offers tariff relief to Audi over Georgia plant
auto-974200daab33.summary: Sources say the United States has signalled to German carmaker Audi that it could ease tariffs as part of discussions about a planned manufacturing facility in the state of Georgia. The talks are reported to involve the potential investment and the trade terms that would apply to vehicles and components produced there. The details could not be independently verified, and it is not clear whether any agreement has been reached.

German carmaker Audi may gain cheaper access to the US market.

impact_points: Germany and Audi's parent company would gain if US tariff relief lowers the cost of building in Georgia.
US trade policy and Georgia's industrial investment prospects could shift depending on whether the arrangement is finalised.

auto-52cc4881d42f.headline: Rights groups oppose UAE's UN secretary-general nominee over Sudan war stance
auto-52cc4881d42f.summary: Sudanese diaspora members and international human rights monitors have criticised Lana Nusseibeh, the Emirati diplomat nominated by the UAE to succeed António Guterres as UN secretary-general. Critics point to her rejection of claims that the UAE backs the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in Sudan, and say her candidacy undermines accountability for atrocities, including the October 2025 attack on El Fasher that the UN said bore hallmarks of genocide. Nusseibeh has said she would back UN fact-finding work on Sudan and has taken leave from her UAE post to show independence. She would need nine Security Council votes and no veto from a permanent member, and no candidate has yet cleared that bar.

actors.why: Its nominee faces criticism over alleged backing of the RSF in Sudan
Civilians and activists fear a UN leader defending Sudan's abusers

impact_points: The UAE faces reputational damage and scrutiny over its alleged support for the RSF and its nominee.

auto-1c67b2feb0e1.headline: Iran says its air force forced away a foreign jet near Hormuz
auto-1c67b2feb0e1.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Aerospace Force says it intercepted a jet it called hostile near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on a Thursday night, and that the aircraft was forced to leave. Iranian media reported the interception, and separate reports described several explosions in nearby waters off Sirik and Qeshm. The article is based on Iranian state-linked reporting and does not identify the aircraft's origin, and the claims could not be independently verified from the text provided. The incident adds to tensions around one of the world's most important shipping routes.

actors.why: Iran reports intercepting a hostile jet and blasts in its waters.

impact_points: Iran faces a security incident in the Strait of Hormuz, a sensitive waterway for global oil shipments.

auto-72b89078a7ab.headline: Drone strike sets fire to Russian refinery in Novokuibyshevsk
auto-72b89078a7ab.summary: A fire broke out at an oil refinery in Novokuibyshevsk, in Russia's Samara Oblast, after a drone attack on the morning of 30 October. Telegram channels reported the blaze and said the plant makes jet fuel used by Russian forces. Residents reported explosions and air defence activity, and an air-raid alert was officially issued around 06:00, after the attack had already begun. The refinery, owned by the Rosneft group since 2007, has an annual capacity of roughly 8.8 million tonnes of oil. The article's details come from unofficial local reports and were not independently confirmed.

Drone strike on Russian energy infrastructure, a potential military gain

impact_points: Russia faces disruption to fuel output, including jet fuel for its Aerospace Forces, from the refinery fire.
Rosneft, the refinery's owner, is exposed to lost processing capacity and repair costs at a plant handling about 8.8 million tonnes yearly.

auto-6a2882ffe652.headline: Australia's defence minister says China's military buildup is pressuring Southeast Asia
auto-6a2882ffe652.summary:
Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said China's military expansion, which he called the largest conventional buildup since World War II, is creating pressure across Southeast Asia. Speaking at the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus in Cebu, Philippines, he urged like-minded partners to deepen cooperation and stressed that shared rules give middle powers like Australia their influence.

The meeting was overshadowed by a dispute between China and the Philippines. Beijing accused Manila of blocking its attendance, and China's defence minister skipped the event, sending only a defence attaché. Tensions in the South China Sea, including incidents at Scarborough Shoal and Second Thomas Shoal, remain high.

actors.why: Faces strategic challenges from China's buildup and urges allied cooperation
Accused of exerting pressure and sent only an attaché to the summit

Part of the Squad group committing to closer defence policy coordination

impact_points: Australia faces growing strategic challenges from China's military build-up, which Marles says is creating regional pressure.
The Philippines is at the centre of a diplomatic row with Beijing and ongoing South China Sea confrontations that strain bilateral relations.

auto-5f4f7e2f4d2a.summary: Diplomats from Group of 20 nations, including those from China and Russia, are heading into talks in Atlanta despite significant disagreements among members. The gathering is a preparatory step for the group's broader agenda, and the rifts described suggest that reaching consensus on contentious issues may be difficult. auto-c1c1f48ed512.headline: Switzerland opens diplomatic office in Pyongyang, its first in North Korea
auto-c1c1f48ed512.summary: Switzerland has formally opened its first diplomatic office in North Korea, with Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis attending the ceremony in Pyongyang on Thursday evening. Cassis and a North Korean diplomat cut a ribbon to mark the occasion. The minister later described the move on social media as a new chapter for Swiss presence in the city and a practical step toward more direct dialogue with Pyongyang. A commemorative plaque dated October 30 and referring to the office's reactivation was also shown in his posts.

Hosts a new Swiss diplomatic office, easing its isolation somewhat

auto-5751e83cdec6.summary: European leaders have gathered in Montreal for an EU-Canada summit aimed at deepening cooperation between the two sides. Talks are expected to cover defence, critical raw materials, space and artificial intelligence. auto-e4a9c49f567c.headline: Israel's election yields no clear majority; Arab-led parties gain ground
auto-e4a9c49f567c.summary: Israel held its first national election since the October 7 attacks and the war in Gaza, and voters turned out in record numbers. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's alliance of right-wing and far-right parties fell short of a majority. The main opposition bloc, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, also lacks enough seats to govern alone. Parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel made unprecedented gains. Netanyahu has ruled out working with Arab-led lists, leaving open whether the opposition could strike a deal with them while military operations in Gaza and the West Bank continue.

auto-071223402a1a.summary: A Russian jet-powered drone struck a crowded platform at the main railway station in Dnipro, Ukraine, killing at least 14 people and wounding at least 14 others, including an 11-year-old boy, according to regional officials. A passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was standing at the platform when it was hit. Russia's military has not commented publicly. Elsewhere, Ukrainian officials reported two teenage girls killed in a missile strike on Chernihiv and three people killed in a drone attack on Kremenchuk, with a day of mourning declared for Chernihiv and Dnipro.

auto-a5c531d7e45a.summary: Israeli troops evacuated residents of a Hebron neighbourhood on Friday while preparing to demolish the homes of the men behind last week's attack at Yehuda Junction. Two soldiers, Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, and Sergeant Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, were killed. The military says the attackers first aimed at the busy Route 35 but turned to a checkpoint when they could not pass it. Separately, a regional council said it would set up eight new outposts in the Hebron Hills in response.

Separately, Albania has introduced fines of up to €5,500 for protesters, prompting public debate and disorder in parliament. The broadcast also covers Israel's political deadlock, its implications for Palestinians, and the escalating Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

auto-1ec36a5c863b.headline: Rubio hosts G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta amid Ukraine and Iran tensions
auto-1ec36a5c863b.summary:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is hosting G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta, Georgia, with talks expected to be difficult. Divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine and the fallout from the conflict with Iran, along with rising energy prices, are expected to dominate. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, who is under international sanctions, is attending, and his encounter with Rubio is drawing close attention. Diplomats expect few breakthroughs and possibly only a US-drafted chair summary rather than a joint declaration, ahead of a December leaders' summit in Miami.

The meeting also comes days before US midterm elections. Energy access and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blocked since strikes began in late February, are on the agenda, and China is expected to object to some wording on free navigation.

actors.why: Hosts talks and seeks a demonstration of American leadership on growth and energy.

auto-08329ba11af8.headline: Israeli siege of Hebron forces nearly 5,000 residents from their homes
auto-08329ba11af8.summary:
Almost 5,000 people have been driven from their homes by an Israeli military lockdown of Hebron in the occupied West Bank, according to Al Jazeera's analysis of municipal data and rights-group figures. The city of about 250,000 is cut off at 10 entry points, and the closure entered its second week. The siege followed a shooting on October 23 in which two Palestinians killed two Israeli soldiers before being shot dead by the army. The Israeli army says the operation aims to search for weapons and arrest suspects, while Defence Minister Israel Katz has said residents will not return until Hamas's infrastructure is dismantled.

The Hebron mayor describes the measures as collective punishment. Most displaced families are staying with relatives or host families nearby, and few have reached official shelters.

Ukrainian air defence said it downed three of the Kh-59/69 missiles and 96 drones, and that drones hit 17 locations while debris fell at five more. The main targets were listed as Kyiv, Poltava and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts. The Air Force did not give the number of ballistic missiles launched or how many were intercepted.

The launches were said to come from Russian regions including Voronezh, Kursk, Bryansk, Belgorod and Oryol, as well as from occupied Donetsk and Crimea. Air defence, electronic warfare and mobile fire groups were involved in the response.
