auto-b77da4478139.headline: Moscow mayor reports 862 drones bound for capital; Samara refinery reportedly hit
auto-b77da4478139.summary:
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 862 Ukrainian drones flew toward the Moscow region from the evening of October 29, with most intercepted at distant approaches and 170 downed nearer the city. He gave no account of damage. Ukrainian monitoring channels and the independent Telegram channel Astra reported strikes on the Novokuibyshevsk refinery in the Samara region, a Rosneft subsidiary that has been hit repeatedly and halted operations before. Regional officials did not confirm the attack, and Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev only said Ukrainian forces were attacking the area on the morning of October 30.

Sobyanin also reported 613 drones in the previous overnight period, with 231 shot down near the capital. The refinery has annual capacity of about 8.8 million tons. The reports remain unverified by independent officials.

actors.why: Russian capital and a major refinery targeted by hundreds of drones
Ukrainian drone campaign against Russian energy and capital targets

impact_points: Russia faces a sustained drone campaign reaching Moscow and the Samara region, with the Novokuibyshevsk refinery reportedly disrupted again.
Rosneft, the refinery's owner, risks further lost output at a plant that already has halted operations after earlier attacks.

auto-2d0bf61ee3da.headline: Binance reports $6.3bn crypto theft, with North Korea suspected
auto-2d0bf61ee3da.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says roughly $6.3bn was stolen in a security breach that appears to be the largest crypto theft on record. The firm halted deposits and withdrawals, froze about $3bn, and said an intruder gained access through an engineer's compromised laptop. Binance has pledged to cover all losses and says user funds are safe. Blockchain intelligence firm TRM assessed with high confidence that North Korea's TraderTraitor unit, linked to the Lazarus Group, carried out the attack. Bitcoin fell about 5 percent afterward.

actors.why: Suspected of carrying out the theft via its linked hacking unit.
Binance is a global exchange; US users and markets are exposed to the fallout.
Binance was founded in China; founder Changpeng Zhao is linked to the firm.

impact_points: Binance and its users face major losses, though the company says it will cover them in full.
North Korea is implicated as the suspected attacker, and TRM says stolen funds can fuel weapons proliferation, making it a security issue.

auto-3fa43a42038f.headline: Drone strike on Dnipro rail platform kills at least 14, officials say
auto-3fa43a42038f.summary: A drone struck a crowded platform at the main railway station in Dnipro, central Ukraine, killing at least 14 people and wounding at least 14 others, including an 11-year-old boy, according to regional officials. A passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was at the platform when it was hit. Russia's military has not commented publicly. Elsewhere, Ukrainian officials reported two teenage girls killed in a missile strike on Chernihiv and three dead in a drone attack on Kremenchuk. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called for more sanctions on Russia and criticised a recent US-Russia deal easing some measures.

actors.why: Civilians killed and wounded in strikes on rail and residential areas
Faces Zelensky's call for more sanctions after the strikes
Zelensky criticises the recent US-Russia deal that eased some sanctions

impact_points: Ukraine faces mounting civilian casualties and disruption to its railway network as attacks on rail infrastructure rise sharply.
Russia faces renewed calls for sanctions from Kyiv, with Zelensky urging further US, European and G7 measures against Moscow.

auto-cd14f3addaac.headline: Gaza health ministry reports 1,574 killed since October 2025 ceasefire
auto-cd14f3addaac.summary: Gaza's health ministry says Israeli attacks killed six Palestinians and wounded 38 in the past day. According to the ministry, Israeli forces have killed at least 1,574 people and wounded 5,687 since a ceasefire took effect on 10 October 2025. The ministry also reports that 845 bodies have been recovered from rubble over the same period. Its cumulative toll for the war that began on 7 October 2023 stands at 74,570 killed and 175,808 wounded. These are the ministry's figures and were not independently verified in the article.

actors.why: Ongoing deaths and injuries from Israeli strikes despite the ceasefire
Accused by Gaza's ministry of continued lethal attacks under the ceasefire

impact_points: Palestinians in Gaza face continued lethal Israeli strikes despite the ceasefire, according to the health ministry's count.
Israel faces scrutiny over its conduct under the ceasefire, as the ministry describes its operations in Gaza as a genocidal war.

auto-4be62b61d7d0.headline: Gulf oil exports recover, yet Brent prices climb on war fears
auto-4be62b61d7d0.summary:
Crude shipments from the Gulf rose to 24.6 million barrels per day in the week to October 18, above the pre-war average, according to the market intelligence firm Kpler. Brent crude nonetheless reached its highest level since April, trading more than 60 percent above pre-war levels and briefly topping $117 a barrel on Friday. Analysts cited fears of renewed fighting, falling stockpiles and sharply higher freight and insurance costs, with shipping shifted to ship-to-ship transfers and pipelines bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.

Analysts quoted in the piece said supply is still well short of its pre-war baseline and that October was the deadliest month for attacks on commercial vessels, with 32 incidents logged. They said prices are unlikely to fall back to around $70 soon without durable de-escalation.

actors.why: Pipeline rerouting keeps exports flowing, though costs and risks rise.
Habshan-Fujairah pipeline and transfers off the UAE sustain exports.
Ongoing war and attacks on shipping keep the region in turmoil.
Fuel prices at home are under pressure from the Iran war.

impact_points: Gulf oil producers such as Saudi Arabia and the UAE keep exporting by rerouting around Hormuz, but at higher cost.
Oil-importing consumers face elevated fuel prices while supply remains about 75 percent of the pre-war baseline.

auto-887d2a345522.headline: Russian glide bomb strike on Izium leaves four dead, fourteen hurt
auto-887d2a345522.summary: A Russian guided aerial bomb attack on the city of Izium, in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, killed four civilians and injured 14 others on 29 October, according to the local city military administration. Rescue work at the strike site was still continuing when the reports were issued, so the death toll could change. Russian forces reportedly dropped three guided bombs on the city that day. The injured are receiving medical care.

actors.why: Civilians killed and injured in Russian bombing of Izium
Russian forces carried out the airstrike on Izium

impact_points: Ukraine and the Izium community face fresh civilian deaths and injuries from Russian bombardment of the Kharkiv region.
Russia's use of guided bombs against towns in Kharkiv region continues to raise pressure on Ukrainian civilians and rescue services.

auto-e5bea6fb3be6.headline: Study finds Trump's trade policies have not narrowed US trade deficit
auto-e5bea6fb3be6.summary: A study by Germany's IW economic institute, seen by Reuters, concludes that President Trump's economic agenda has supported growth and AI investment but has not shrunk the US trade deficit. The goods deficit reached $130 billion in August, above its level two years earlier, despite broad import tariffs. The EU's share of the deficit dropped to 7% from 20%, and China's fell to 14% from 29%. Foreign direct investment inflows fell 8.2% in 2025, and the study says the Iran war is adding to public debt and pushing up interest rates.

actors.why: Deficit persists, job creation lags, debt and interest rates rising
Its share of the US trade deficit fell from 29% to 14%
Its share of the US trade deficit fell from 20% to 7%
Named as the target of the US-Israeli war driving up US debt

impact_points: The United States faces persistent trade imbalances and weaker job creation despite strong growth and investment.
The EU and China have seen their shares of the US trade deficit fall sharply, while rising debt and rates pressure Washington.

auto-df82d90d24f1.headline: Houthis deny drone launch as Saudi coalition reports interception near Mecca
auto-df82d90d24f1.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it shot down a ballistic missile that it said the Houthis had fired toward Saudi Arabia's eastern region early on Thursday. Separately, Saudi civil defence issued two warnings of possible danger, one for Najran and one for the Eastern Province, and later said the threat had passed in both areas. The Houthis have denied launching a drone, according to the report, and the claims were not independently verified in the coverage.

actors.why: Targeted by a missile the coalition says it intercepted, prompting civil alerts
Houthi forces accused of the launch, which they deny, risking escalation

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces renewed missile threats, with civil defence alerts issued across southern and eastern regions.
Yemen's Houthis are under pressure as Saudi Arabia accuses them of firing toward its territory while they deny the drone claim.

auto-f0e6b1c01441.headline: Vance reportedly writes to Iranian security chief to revive talks
auto-f0e6b1c01441.summary: US Vice President JD Vance has reportedly sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Security Council, in an attempt to restart stalled peace negotiations, according to US officials and sources who spoke to the Wall Street Journal. The report, published on a Wednesday, adds that the US had earlier warned several Gulf Arab states to prepare for a brief but intense military operation against Iran following the November midterm elections. The contents of the letter could not be independently verified from the article.

actors.why: Vance seeks renewed talks but Trump threatens to resume war
Faces a potential renewed offensive and pressure to negotiate
Warned to prepare for possible US military action against Iran
Gulf neighbour warned to prepare for a possible US offensive

impact_points: Iran faces renewed pressure over a possible short, intense US military offensive after the midterms.
Gulf Arab states are being asked to prepare for possible US strikes, drawing them into the standoff.

auto-a54874423bf8.headline: Haiti sets election dates as El Salvador deploys troops to find kidnapped soldiers
auto-a54874423bf8.summary:
Haitian authorities have set a timetable for the country's first general election in over ten years, with a first round on July 18 and a runoff on October 4. The vote is planned despite ongoing fighting between state forces and armed gangs, and the country has been without an elected president since Jovenel Moïse was killed in 2021. Electoral officials expect to publish the final candidate list by mid-January, with voter registration closing May 20.

Separately, El Salvador has sent 2,000 troops to Haiti to help locate four of its soldiers seized by gangs two weeks ago. The men were serving with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force when their armoured vehicle was attacked and burned. El Salvador has also extended its participation in the mission until October 2027.

actors.why: Election timetable set, but gang violence threatens the process and stability
Four soldiers kidnapped; troops deployed and mission commitment extended

impact_points: Haiti faces a planned vote amid gang violence, a test of whether a return to elected government is feasible.
El Salvador's soldiers are held captive, and its deployment ties its forces to the anti-gang mission until 2027.

auto-d71b8262c14e.headline: South Korea and Germany's leaders to meet in Seoul on economic ties
auto-d71b8262c14e.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung was set to host German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Seoul on Thursday for a summit aimed at deepening economic cooperation. It is Merz's first trip to South Korea since taking office and the first visit by a German chancellor there in three years. The agenda includes batteries, semiconductors and artificial intelligence, as well as defence and arms industry collaboration and regional issues. Merz will also address a German business conference during his two-day stay. The report is based on Seoul's presidential office and Yonhap; the leaders' meeting will be their third since Merz took office.

actors.why: Seeks expanded economic and defence cooperation with a major European partner
Chancellor pursues new markets and industrial partnerships in Asia

impact_points: South Korea gains closer economic and defence ties with Germany in key technology sectors.
Germany's businesses could expand investment and trade in South Korea's battery, chip and AI industries.

auto-b88e76405222.headline: Russian strikes hit Kyiv energy sites as aid heads to besieged Oleshky
auto-b88e76405222.summary: Russia says its forces struck energy infrastructure in and around Kyiv on Friday, while an aid convoy with food and medical supplies began moving overnight toward Oleshky, a town in southern Ukraine held by Russian forces. Both sides' human rights commissioners are overseeing a localised ceasefire there, and residents were allowed to leave until mid-afternoon local time. Russia's defence ministry also reported strikes in Dnipropetrovsk, Odesa port facilities and cargo vessels. The day before, a drone attack on a Dnipro railway platform killed at least 14 people, according to officials.

actors.why: Energy sites in Kyiv hit and a deadly railway attack in Dnipro.
Its forces struck Ukrainian energy sites; it gains a rare cooperation deal.
Russia is seeking favour with Washington before possible talks.

impact_points: Ukraine faces renewed strikes on energy infrastructure in Kyiv while Oleshky residents gain a rare window to evacuate.
Russia seeks to show cooperation with Washington ahead of possible three-way talks, according to the article's interpretation.

auto-ee00ca1a425a.headline: Oleshky residents given until Friday to leave as humanitarian aid truce takes hold
auto-ee00ca1a425a.summary: Russian and Ukrainian human rights commissioners say routes into Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, have been cleared of mines and a humanitarian convoy is ready to move. Civilians who want to leave the Russian-occupied city have until 2 p.m. on Friday, October 30, and aid distribution to those staying is set to start after 2:30 p.m. that day. Delegations from Ukraine, Russia and the United States were gathering to coordinate the next steps, with journalists from all three countries present. A ceasefire brokered with the involvement of U.S. first lady Melania Trump began October 27 and runs until late on November 1.

actors.why: Gains a chance to evacuate civilians and deliver aid under the truce.
Oversees the occupied city and the convoy route, under pressure to show humanitarian cooperation.
Brokered the deal via Melania Trump and hosts delegations coordinating the mission.

impact_points: Ukraine and Russia both face the humanitarian strain of trapped civilians in Oleshky, where residents have lacked food, power and medicine.
Civilians wishing to reach Ukrainian-held territory may first be routed through Russia, raising questions about their path and safety.

auto-ac078d63a512.headline: Spanish authorities continue probing causes of fatal Toledo rail accident
auto-ac078d63a512.summary: Spanish investigators are still working to establish what caused a deadly train crash near Toledo, in central Spain. The inquiry remains open, and no conclusive findings on the cause have been announced in the coverage available. The accident is being followed as part of a broader live news feed on European affairs.

actors.why: Domestic fatal rail crash under investigation, raising safety questions for national authorities

impact_points: Spain faces scrutiny over rail safety as investigators work to explain the fatal Toledo crash.
Passengers and families affected by the crash are waiting for answers on how the accident happened.

auto-3d20c8a5a5da.headline: Putin hosts African leaders in Moscow for Russia-Africa summit
auto-3d20c8a5a5da.summary:
Russia is hosting a two-day summit in Moscow with delegations from 48 African countries, co-chaired by Vladimir Putin and the African Union's current chair, Burundi's Evariste Ndayishimiye. Agenda items include trade, defence, energy, food security and technology, and the meeting is expected to adopt a final declaration and a partnership plan covering 2027 to 2029.

According to Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov, 22 heads of state are attending, fewer than at the 2019 first summit. Analysts see Russia's security footprint in Africa as growing faster than its trade, and Amnesty International has urged leaders to press Moscow over the recruitment of Africans to fight in Ukraine.

actors.why: Hosts summit to expand influence and security ties despite Western sanctions
Egyptian president scheduled to meet Putin during the summit
Ethiopian prime minister scheduled to meet Putin during the summit
Burkina Faso's leader attends, tied to Russia's growing security role
Niger's leader attends, tied to Russia's growing security role
Kenya faces diplomatic concern over recruitment of Kenyans to fight in Ukraine

impact_points: African states attending gain a platform for trade, energy and defence deals as Western sanctions squeeze Russia's economy.
Russia strengthens its influence and military footprint across Africa, while facing criticism over recruitment of Africans for its war in Ukraine.

auto-637febf08978.headline: Democratic leaders rally behind Michigan Senate hopeful El-Sayed amid Trump attacks
auto-637febf08978.summary: Democratic figures, including Bernie Sanders, Barack Obama and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, have campaigned with Abdul El-Sayed, the party's nominee in Michigan's closely watched US Senate race. The support follows a bitter split over his primary win in August, which he secured over a moderate pro-Israel rival backed by much of the party establishment. Donald Trump has repeatedly attacked El-Sayed with false claims about his faith and name, and Republicans have aired ads using his full name. Polls show a tight race against Republican Mike Rogers, and the outcome could affect control of the Senate. Some Democrats' backing remains qualified, with disagreements on Israel noted.

actors.why: Michigan Senate race could decide chamber control; domestic political contest

impact_points: The United States Democratic Party gains momentum in Michigan, a state that could help decide Senate control.
Republicans, including Mike Rogers' campaign, face pressure as the race tightens and attacks on El-Sayed intensify.

auto-44d668bf6d31.headline: UK budget cuts put green heating targets at risk, experts warn
auto-44d668bf6d31.summary:
Experts say Britain is unlikely to meet its clean heating goals after the chancellor, John Healey, announced more than £3bn in cuts to the energy department's budget. Much of the saving is being redirected to higher defence spending. The heat pump subsidy scheme, which offers households up to £7,500, is among the casualties, with its funding now set to rise only with inflation rather than as previously planned.

Critics argue the changes signal a retreat from the renewables agenda pursued under former energy secretary Ed Miliband and his successor, Miatta Fahnbulleh. Energy department sources counter that longer-term reforms will still favour cleaner power, and allies of the two secretaries say the government's green commitments remain intact.

actors.why: Heat pump subsidies cut and green targets threatened as funds move to defence

impact_points: UK households considering heat pumps face reduced government support, which could slow installations well below the 250,000 a year target.
Britain's 2030 clean power and emissions goals face greater doubt as funds shift from renewables, hydrogen and carbon capture to defence.

auto-222983abd997.headline: Ukrainian delegation reaches occupied Oleshky as aid and evacuation begin
auto-222983abd997.summary: A Ukrainian delegation has entered Oleshky, a town in Kherson Oblast that is under temporary Russian occupation, according to lawmaker Davyd Arakhamiia. He said the group arrived safely and that evacuation and aid distribution had started, with further details promised later. Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said he was on the ground in the town, speaking with residents about their needs. He said a ceasefire had held for 80 hours and remained in place.

actors.why: Ukrainian delegation enters occupied town to evacuate people and deliver aid
Russian forces' local ceasefire allows the delegation access to Oleshky

impact_points: Ukraine gains a chance to move civilians out and deliver aid to residents of occupied Oleshky.
Residents of Oleshky, who face shortages under occupation, may receive relief if the ceasefire holds.

auto-ae40c78a5ce4.headline: Dockworkers across 22 countries plan October 30 strike against Gaza war
auto-ae40c78a5ce4.summary: Dock and port workers in 22 countries are preparing a coordinated strike on October 30 to protest the war in Gaza and what they call imperialist conflicts. The action involves more than 25 unions and over 110 ports, with some countries, including France, Italy, India, Greece and Turkey, calling 24-hour stoppages and others planning shorter walkouts. Organisers say their main demand is an immediate end to what they describe as genocide against Palestinians. A campaign group, No Harbour for Genocide, says it tracked 315 shipments of components for Israeli arms maker Elbit Systems through 56 ports in 29 countries, and expects over $2bn in cargo to be held up.

Strike aims to press for an end to the Gaza war and recognition of Palestinian statehood
Multiple Italian ports and a national general strike call are involved
Piraeus port and wider Greek unions are central to the action
Marseille port and a 24-hour strike are part of the action
Tangier port, with alleged Israel-bound shipment links, joins a short strike

impact_points: Israel and Elbit Systems could face delays to arms component shipments routed through the 56 affected ports.
Ports in Italy, France, Greece and Morocco with alleged links to Israel-bound weapons shipments are expected to see significant disruption.

auto-2400893b26be.headline: EU and Canada pursue closer ties amid member-state disagreement over associate status
auto-2400893b26be.summary: Ahead of an EU-Canada summit in Montreal, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she wants relations raised to the highest possible level and floated associate membership of the bloc for Canada. Several EU capitals, led by Germany, objected to the term, and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz instead announced an "Alliance for the Future" without mentioning it. European Council President António Costa tried to bridge the split, backing the ambition while playing down the label. Prime Minister Mark Carney said the naming did not matter, and the two sides are expected to publish a joint statement describing a relationship "short of full membership".

actors.why: Gains deeper EU partnership and a path toward greater sovereignty from US pressure
Seeks closer ties with Canada but faces internal division over the proposed status

impact_points: Canada gains closer EU ties and a new partnership framework as it seeks greater independence from Washington.
EU member states remain divided, with Germany and others wary of an untested status whose legal form is undefined.

auto-0b09b7e59c58.headline: Cameroonian relatives demand return of men recruited to fight for Russia
auto-0b09b7e59c58.summary: Families of Cameroonian men lured to Russia with promises of work have called for their return after many ended up fighting in Ukraine. A group called Bring Back Our Sons and Brothers held a peaceful march to the Russian Embassy in Yaoundé, urging Russia and Cameroon to shut down covert recruitment networks. Citing a report by the collective All Eyes on Wagner, at least 1,417 Africans have reportedly been recruited into the Russian military, with over 300 said to be dead; these figures could not be independently verified here. Relatives say they have had no word on whether their men are alive.

actors.why: Families lose sons to covert recruitment, prompting public protest and calls for action.

Recruits from Cameroon are fighting in Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Russia is under pressure from Cameroonian families and campaigners to repatriate recruits and end the schemes.

auto-b13e9878acec.headline: TotalEnergies reports record quarterly profit while holding French pump prices below rivals
auto-b13e9878acec.summary: French oil and gas company TotalEnergies has reported record profits for the quarter ending in September. The firm says it has kept fuel prices at its French petrol stations lower than those of competitors. The report comes as large protests over the cost of living are expected across France this weekend, and drivers are asking whether pump prices could fall further.

actors.why: Consumers face high living costs; TotalEnergies keeps some pump prices lower
European energy prices and profit debates are a wider concern

impact_points: French motorists and households facing high living costs may benefit if TotalEnergies keeps pump prices below rivals.
France's cost-of-living protests put pressure on energy companies to justify record profits while fuel stays expensive.

auto-3052f0a59a06.headline: Oleshky evacuation begins under short ceasefire in Russian-held Kherson
auto-3052f0a59a06.summary:
An evacuation from Oleshky, a Ukrainian city under Russian occupation, has started after Russian and Ukrainian officials confirmed the operation. A truce covering the Kherson frontline region, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, allowed Russian sappers to clear mines from the road out. Residents wishing to leave have a four-hour window, with a convoy of 25 buses able to carry up to 750 people, plus ambulances. Several hundred people are reported to be staying despite severe shortages of power, gas and water.

Evacuees will travel through Russian-occupied land to Anapa in Russia, fly to Gomel in Belarus, then cross into Ukraine's Chernihiv region. The ceasefire runs until the end of 1 November.

impact_points: Ukraine faces the loss of residents from Oleshky, though its ombudsman says humanitarian aid will reach those who remain.

auto-533f6a713214.headline: G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta face splits over Ukraine and Iran
auto-533f6a713214.summary:
Foreign ministers from the G20 economies are gathering in Atlanta on 30 and 31 October, hosted by the United States, which holds this year's rotating presidency. Analysts and diplomats expect deep divisions over the wars in Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran to make joint statements hard to reach. South Africa has not been invited, while Russia's foreign minister Sergei Lavrov will attend, adding to the friction. The US agenda focuses on energy, supply chains and critical minerals, with a Pax Silica initiative aimed at China's rare earths dominance.

Experts said any broader consensus may come later, through smaller coalitions, and noted that the Quad group also meets in Atlanta in the coming days. The European Union's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas plans to press for more support for Ukraine.

auto-32d742be69a6.headline: Russian missile strike in Chernihiv kills two teenage girls
auto-32d742be69a6.summary:
A Russian missile attack hit the Ukrainian city of Chernihiv, killing two teenage girls, according to Ukrainian officials. Regional military authorities said the weapon used was a Banderol cruise missile, a comparatively cheap jet-powered munition that can circle over an area before hitting its target. Cars, homes and businesses were damaged, and rescuers were seen putting out fires and treating casualties at the scene.

The strike occurred while a separate, US-brokered local ceasefire was reported to be holding around Oleshky in Russian-occupied Kherson region. Ukrainian and Russian human rights ombudsmen said that truce had lasted more than 30 hours without incident, and aims to open routes for aid and evacuation.

Missile strike on Ukrainian city; local truce may ease pressure

auto-3a7a29b1919f.headline: US Army general removed and Alaska Senate contest draws spoiler accusations
auto-3a7a29b1919f.summary: Two separate US stories were covered in one NPR segment. One concerns an accusation that a candidate in Alaska's Senate race is acting as a spoiler, meaning a contender whose presence could split votes and shift the outcome. The full text was not reviewed, so further details such as names, dates and the stated reasons could not be verified here.

auto-4d615275370e.headline: Qatari envoys in Tehran as mediators seek to restart US-Iran talks
auto-4d615275370e.summary: A Qatari delegation led by a senior adviser to Qatar's prime minister arrived in Tehran on Friday, according to Iranian state news agency IRNA, to discuss bilateral ties and regional developments with Iranian officials. The visit follows reports that US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei, reportedly focused on a possible framework for negotiations. Qatar and Pakistan are mediating efforts to revive talks after an April ceasefire, and Iran says it is discussing a plan with both to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

auto-f9b626536833.headline: Ukraine reports over 1,000 Russian boats hit by drones this year
auto-f9b626536833.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence says its forces have destroyed or disabled 1,039 Russian boats and speedboats with drones since January 2026. The ministry said July was the peak month, with more than 230 vessels struck, and that 67 more boats were hit between 1 and 25 October. Each strike is recorded in the Delta battlefield awareness system and verified by the Brave1 defence innovation cluster, according to the ministry. Officials argue the attacks weaken Russia's ability to control waterways and move troops, equipment and supplies. auto-586f705a164c.headline: US Central Command disputes Iranian claims of tanker mine strikes near Hormuz
auto-586f705a164c.summary: US Central Command has rejected Iranian media reports that commercial ships are striking sea mines while passing through the Strait of Hormuz, calling the claims false. In a post on X, the US military said all internationally recognised main transit routes through the strait have been cleared of mines by American forces. It added that thousands of commercial vessels have used those lanes safely and continue to do so. The reports being disputed came from Iranian-controlled outlets over recent days and weeks; the US statement does not independently confirm or deny any specific incident.

auto-02c0bee807d0.headline: Kremlin says Europe excluded from Abu Dhabi talks; Ukraine seeks wider involvement

Russia's Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said European countries would not take part in the next round of talks with Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi, after a phone call involving Putin and the leaders of Finland and Norway. Finnish President Alexander Stubb later said European countries would be involved in the November talks, a claim that conflicts with the Kremlin account. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said the trilateral talks are set for November 6 to 10 in the UAE and that Kyiv wants Europe included.

In The Hague, Zelenskyy met Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who pledged an extra 500 million euros for Ukrainian military needs, and the Dutch government announced wider support worth 1.2 billion euros over three years. Britain also announced a further 10 billion pound package, including 500 million pounds in military aid for air defences.

actors.why: Talks proceed without Europe, though the Kremlin's position is contested

auto-e1457ac2172b.summary:
Israeli forces demolished the homes of two Palestinians who killed two Israeli soldiers at a Hebron checkpoint on October 23, both of whom were shot dead during the attack. The demolitions form part of a wider operation that has forced over 3,000 Palestinians from their homes, according to the report. Palestinian officials say Prime Minister Netanyahu is using the campaign to build support before Israel's general election on Tuesday, while the military says it will keep acting offensively against attacks.

Local officials also report other homes, shops, roads and factories destroyed in Hebron, and most entrances to the city have been closed. UN human rights chief Volker Türk voiced serious concern about disproportionate force and possible ethnic cleansing. Separately, settler attacks on Palestinian olive harvesters were recorded near Ramallah, which the military said it had responded to.

actors.why: Thousands displaced, homes demolished and city entrances closed in Hebron
Military operation after soldiers killed, but drawing UN criticism and election-period scrutiny
Settlement expansion and settler violence criticised as illegal, drawing international concern

impact_points: Palestinian families in Hebron face displacement, lost homes and restricted movement, including access to medical care.
Israel faces international criticism from UN rights bodies, while its government says the operation responds to deadly attacks on soldiers.

auto-7cc65a4b4cc0.headline: Slovak prosecutor reopens case over 2023 jet and air defense donation to Ukraine
auto-7cc65a4b4cc0.summary: Slovakia's Prosecutor General, Maros Zilinka, has reopened a criminal case against former prime minister Eduard Heger and former defense minister Jaroslav Nad. The case concerns their government's approval in March 2023 of a donation of 13 MiG-29 fighter jets and part of its KUB air defense systems to Ukraine. Zilinka said the earlier investigation, which had been closed in February, was shut too soon and that the facts were not fully established. He has moved supervision of the case to a regional prosecutor in Trencin. Heger and Nad deny the sabotage and abuse-of-power allegations originally brought by the current government of Prime Minister Robert Fico.

actors.why: Former leaders face renewed criminal probe over the jet donation
Donated jets were delivered to Ukraine, but the probe threatens that support's legacy
Probe revisits Ukrainian access to Soviet-era jets Moscow opposed

impact_points: Slovakia's former leaders Heger and Nad face renewed legal jeopardy over a donation that supported Ukraine's defense.
Ukraine and its Western partners could see the case as political pressure over military aid from Slovakia's current government.

auto-b702e8969c9e.headline: Attacks on a camp in Ethiopia reportedly leave at least 15 dead
auto-b702e8969c9e.summary: Sources report that strikes on a camp in Ethiopia have killed at least 15 people. The reporting does not establish with certainty who carried out the attack, and the details offered are limited. The incident adds to concerns about violence affecting civilians in the country.

actors.why: Deadly strikes on a camp inside Ethiopia; civilians killed and security strained

impact_points: Ethiopia faces another deadly episode of violence, with civilians in camps among those exposed to harm.
Displaced people and aid operations in the affected area may face heightened risk and disruption.

auto-f5ceba65384e.headline: Binance hit by record $6.3 billion crypto theft, linked to North Korea
auto-f5ceba65384e.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has suffered a cyber theft worth about $6.3 billion, which is described as the largest of its kind. Blockchain intelligence firms have tied the attack to North Korea. By Thursday evening in the United States, a joint effort by major crypto platforms had reportedly frozen around $3 billion of the stolen funds as investigators tried to trace and secure them.

actors.why: Accused by blockchain firms of being behind the heist, drawing scrutiny and possible sanctions.
Crypto platforms there helped freeze roughly half the stolen funds during the tracing effort.

impact_points: Binance and its customers face heavy losses after the record cyber theft of digital assets.
North Korea is implicated, adding to international concern over state-linked crypto hacking and sanctions evasion.

auto-8674c048d1d8.headline: Lebanese court charges 13 over seized Hezbollah explosives truck
auto-8674c048d1d8.summary:
A Lebanese military court has brought charges against 13 people linked to a truck carrying explosives that authorities seized at a checkpoint on the Beirut to Bekaa Valley highway earlier this month. Two suspects are in custody, while the other 11, five of them known only by nicknames, were charged in absentia. The charges include undermining state security and illegal weapons possession. Hezbollah later said the 780 kilograms of explosives were meant for use against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon and asked for their return.

The case reflects a sharp change since March, when the government outlawed Hezbollah's military activities during the latest war with Israel. Hezbollah has not accepted that decision.

actors.why: Government pursuing charges against armed group, testing state authority over Hezbollah
Its ally Hezbollah faces seizure, prosecution and pressure to disarm
Hezbollah's stockpile seized, though Israeli forces still occupy south Lebanon

impact_points: Lebanon's government faces a direct test of its authority over Hezbollah's armed activities and arms.
Hezbollah, backed by Iran, faces legal pressure and public anger over the seized weapons shipment.

auto-34fe22865556.headline: Aden residents stockpile supplies and plan escape routes amid Houthi missile strikes
auto-34fe22865556.summary: Residents of Aden, Yemen's southern port city, are preparing for possible renewed war after a series of Houthi missile and drone attacks this month. The Iran-backed group has claimed strikes on the city's international airport, military camps, the port and the presidential palace, which houses the government. The fighting follows a September offensive by the Houthis against government-held western areas, including the port of Mocha and the Bab al-Mandeb strait. Residents describe stockpiling food, mapping escape routes and families keeping children away from schools and windows, while the airport's disruption has forced flight cancellations and diversions.

actors.why: Missile and drone attacks on Aden disrupt airport, port and daily life
Houthis, Iran-backed group, are the attackers in the offensive
Saudi Arabia backs the pro-government forces opposing the Houthis

impact_points: Yemen's government and the residents of Aden face rising risk of renewed large-scale violence and displacement.
Civilians in Aden face possible price spikes and supply shortages if the port or airport is struck.

auto-98f19a43e01e.headline: Omani navy rescues 25 crew from a ship off Musandam
auto-98f19a43e01e.summary: Oman's navy has taken 25 crew members off a vessel near the Musandam peninsula, the northern tip of Oman that overlooks the Strait of Hormuz. The evacuation was carried out by Omani naval forces. Further details about the cause of the incident and the vessel's condition were not available at the time of writing.

actors.why: Omani navy carried out the rescue of 25 crew from its waters

impact_points: Oman is affected as its navy carried out the evacuation of 25 people from a vessel in its waters.
The crew members and their families are affected by the rescue, which removed them from the vessel safely.

auto-9d7bf1a6a645.headline: Analyst warns planned Ukraine-Russia-US talks risk rewarding Moscow
auto-9d7bf1a6a645.summary: Trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States are planned for Abu Dhabi in early November. An analyst writing for the Kyiv Independent argues that a return to negotiations should not be mistaken for real progress toward peace. The piece says Moscow has agreed to attend but has not shown readiness to compromise, and it highlights territory as the first sticking point. It warns that pressure to secure a quick ceasefire could force Ukraine to trade land, and that vague security guarantees, drawing on the 1994 Budapest Memorandum and the Minsk agreements, could leave Ukraine exposed again.

actors.why: Pressed to cede territory and accept vague security guarantees under US pressure
Agreed to resume talks while keeping demands that constrain Ukrainian sovereignty
Seen as impatient for a quick deal that could sideline European input
Expects a role in shaping any settlement but has limited influence at the table

impact_points: Ukraine faces pressure to give up land for a ceasefire that could let Russia regroup for another offensive.
Europe risks footing the bill for Ukraine's defense and security while having limited say in the talks.

auto-c0f80eb49a83.headline: French port strike unions seek better conditions amid debate over military spending
auto-c0f80eb49a83.summary: A France 24 video segment looks at an international dockworkers' strike and whether unions can influence Europe's growing defence investment as well as its effects on automation. Economist Renaud Foucart of Lancaster University, speaking in the piece, says port workers hold strong leverage because of their central place in global supply chains. He doubts they can redirect military policy, but expects them to win concessions on automation and working conditions. The article itself is brief and the segment's full text was not available for detail.

actors.why: Port strike puts pressure on French ports and labour relations
Debate touches on Europe's expanding military investment

impact_points: France's port workers could secure better pay and conditions through their supply-chain leverage.
European governments face pressure over automation and military spending as dockworker action continues.

auto-5bfbfb716047.headline: NATO commander says Patriot interceptor deliveries to Ukraine are on track
auto-5bfbfb716047.summary: Alexus Grynkewich, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe, said the United States is still supplying Ukraine with Patriot air defence interceptors and other weapons paid for by European allies. He told Bloomberg that none of the items in the PURL package funded by those allies had been held up, and that a delivery had arrived within the past week. He did not disclose quantities or missile types. He also said all third-party transfer requests submitted to Washington had been approved, and that work on the content of future PURL packages is ongoing.

actors.why: Patriot interceptor deliveries are continuing and strengthen Ukraine's air defence
Washington is approving third-party transfers and keeping the supply flowing
European allies are funding PURL packages that are arriving without delay

impact_points: Ukraine is receiving air defence supplies on schedule, which bears on its ability to counter Russian missile and drone attacks.
European allies funding the PURL initiative see their paid-for weapons reaching Kyiv, while the United States remains the supplier.

auto-bdab4019642a.headline: Pentagon puts Iran war cost at $47.1bn ahead of US midterms
auto-bdab4019642a.summary: The US Pentagon has told lawmakers that the war against Iran has cost American taxpayers at least $47.1 billion so far, according to an estimate disclosed days before the midterm elections. The figure, covering costs up to October 16, includes about $29 billion to replace used munitions and spending by the Air Force, Navy, Army and other commands. The Pentagon's total does not yet include repairs to damaged Middle East bases or fuel costs. Democratic senators have accused the administration of hiding the true cost, and Trump had not commented on the figure.

actors.why: Taxpayers face at least $47.1bn in costs and political pressure before midterms
Targeted in the war and its shipping lanes disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz closure
Co-belligerent with the US in the war on Iran

impact_points: The United States faces mounting taxpayer costs and strain on munitions stockpiles from the Iran war.
Iran and Gulf energy markets are affected by the disruption to Strait of Hormuz shipping, raising global energy costs.

auto-dc057eeb6e70.headline: Former Israeli PM Barak says Netanyahu lost badly in election
auto-dc057eeb6e70.summary: Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak, speaking to France 24 from Tel Aviv, argued that Benjamin Netanyahu was defeated in this week's Israeli election rather than having won. He said opponents of Netanyahu took 67 seats when Arab parties are counted, against 53 for the right-wing and far-right coalition. Barak urged opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to consider working with Arab parties. He also dismissed Netanyahu's claims of Qatari funding for an Arab party as a diversion from a corruption probe, and warned that Netanyahu might strike Iran to stay in power.

actors.why: Post-election coalition deadlock and a possible Iran strike threaten stability
Faces possible Israeli military action that Barak says Netanyahu may consider
Named in Netanyahu camp's funding claims, which Doha denies

impact_points: Israel faces a contested political outcome, with coalition arithmetic depending on whether Arab parties are included.
Iran could face an Israeli strike, which Barak says Netanyahu may pursue for domestic political reasons.

auto-9b2dc2c55507.headline: Russia's foreign minister to attend G20 talks in Atlanta despite US sanctions
auto-9b2dc2c55507.summary:
Russia's Foreign Ministry says Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov will attend a G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on October 30 and 31. Moscow says he plans to promote ideas for a multipolar world. Lavrov has been under US sanctions since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, though he has visited the United States several times since then for UN General Assembly sessions.

A G20 leaders' summit is set for Miami in mid-December, and Putin has been invited. The Kremlin has not confirmed his attendance. Sources cited by The Atlantic say Trump hopes Putin and Zelensky will sign a peace deal there.

actors.why: Lavrov gets a G20 platform to push multipolar proposals despite sanctions
Hosts G20 meetings and faces questions over sanctioned Russian visitors
Could be affected by a possible Putin-Zelensky peace deal pushed at the summit

impact_points: Russia gains a diplomatic platform at the G20 while still under US sanctions on its foreign minister.
Ukraine and its supporters face the prospect of Putin being hosted in the US amid peace efforts.

auto-74789cb94ea7.headline: Putin pitches Russia as Africa's alternative to Western partners at Moscow summit
auto-74789cb94ea7.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted African leaders at the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow. He argued that Russia makes a better partner than Western countries, saying Russian firms work in Africa on equal terms while accusing the West of still seeking to extract the continent's resources. Russia also stressed the idea of a "multipolar world" and, according to the report, is seeking backing from Global South countries as it faces Western pressure over its war in Ukraine. Trade and security ties with several African states have grown in recent years.

actors.why: Seeks African backing and new trade and security partners amid Western pressure.
Western partners are criticised by Moscow as seeking to exploit African resources.

impact_points: Russia gains diplomatic leverage and a wider base of support while under Western pressure over Ukraine.
African states hosting the summit weigh security and trade ties with Moscow against their existing Western relationships.

auto-8ba888ef68b2.headline: Rosatom says Russia is negotiating large nuclear plant projects with four African nations
auto-8ba888ef68b2.summary: Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom has said Moscow is holding discussions with four African countries about building large nuclear power stations. The details of the talks, including which countries are involved and the timeline for any agreements, could not be independently verified from the available reporting. The announcement points to Russia's continued effort to expand its civil nuclear business and its influence across the African continent.

actors.why: Rosatom pursues new nuclear export deals and expanded African influence
Russia's African nuclear push could shape regional energy partnerships

impact_points: Russia gains a possible new export market for its nuclear technology and construction services through Rosatom.
African states in the talks could gain access to large-scale power generation, though they would take on major financial and technical commitments.

auto-fa192c07cee3.headline: Africans recruited for Russia's war in Ukraine; Tunisian families search for missing men
auto-fa192c07cee3.summary: A France 24 video report says more than 1,400 Africans have been enlisted to fight for Russia in Ukraine since 2023. The recruitment was not on the agenda of a Russia-Africa summit, where African leaders and Russian officials discussed security, trade and political ties. Families of several men from Tunisia, who had gone to Russia for work or study, say they still do not know what happened to them.

Faces fighting involving foreign recruits from African countries

African countries and their citizens face the risk of recruitment into a foreign war, with the report describing this as a sensitive issue.

auto-5da9b4f8b162.headline: EU and Canada set to deepen partnership at Montréal summit
auto-5da9b4f8b162.summary: The European Union and Canada are holding a summit in Montréal, Quebec, to widen cooperation on trade, investment, supply chains, artificial intelligence, climate, security and the Arctic. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has argued the two are complementary, and Canada's integration into EU programmes such as Horizon and Erasmus is also on the agenda. Critical raw materials and liquefied natural gas, which Canada is ready to supply more of, are priority topics, and Ukraine's funding gap is another. The article presents the closer ties as a response to strained relations with the United States under Donald Trump. A last-minute German push to drop the phrase "associate membership" from the joint declaration was reported ahead of the meeting.

actors.why: Gains new partners and trade and energy outlets amid strained US ties
Secures alternative allies, raw materials and LNG, reducing China dependence
Loses its traditional closest-ally status as partners draw closer elsewhere
Seeks help covering a roughly 70 billion euro budget gap as Russia escalates
Pushed to remove associate membership wording from the joint declaration

impact_points: Canada gains a closer role with the EU, reducing its heavy reliance on the US economy.
The EU seeks minerals and energy suppliers to lessen dependence on China and bring down prices.

auto-d745548e1ca8.headline: Senators reportedly briefed on US plans to resume strikes against Iran
auto-d745548e1ca8.summary: An Al Jazeera opinion piece argues that the fighting that Israel and the United States began against Iran on February 28 has paused but not ended, and that a renewed round is likely. The author says both governments are driven by long-term goals, pointing to Israeli leaders' stated aims and US policy toward Iran since the 1950s. The piece cites reported signs of renewed joint strikes, including a visit by War Secretary Pete Hegseth to Israel and reported Israeli targeting of Iranian petrochemical and nuclear sites. It also notes the continuing US naval blockade of Iranian ports and Iran's warnings of retaliation and a possible global energy crisis.

actors.why: Faces renewed strikes, a naval blockade and threats to its nuclear and petrochemical sites
Leaders reportedly plan renewed strikes and seek regime change, with Netanyahu campaigning on it
Accused of planning renewed war and of driving policy through declining power and blockade
Gulf host states risk becoming targets because of US bases, as the author argues

impact_points: Iran faces the prospect of renewed strikes on its petrochemical and nuclear sites, plus a blockade of its ports.
Gulf countries hosting US bases could become targets, and global energy markets risk disruption through the Strait of Hormuz.

auto-1951417ecaf6.headline: Satellite images show two Su-34 jets destroyed at Russian Marinovka airbase
auto-1951417ecaf6.summary: Ukrainian open-source intelligence groups AviVector and CyberBoroshno have published satellite photographs of Marinovka airfield in Russia's Volgograd Oblast. The images, taken on 30 October, show wreckage of two Su-34 fighter-bombers in parking areas near the hangars. The damage followed a Ukrainian Neptune missile strike on the base on 29 October, which the groups say targeted the aircraft at their usual parking positions. The claims are based on the imagery and the groups' own assessments, which were not independently verified in the reporting.

Claimed successful Neptune strike deep inside Russia, shown by satellite imagery

impact_points: Russia loses two Su-34 fighter-bombers, a direct blow to its frontline strike capacity.
Ukraine gains a claimed success showing its missiles can reach deep into Russian-held airfields in Volgograd Oblast.

auto-8dbda04b78fd.headline: Algerian troops reach Niger, its first foreign deployment since 1973
auto-8dbda04b78fd.summary: An Algerian army convoy has reached Arlit, a uranium mining town in northwestern Niger, according to ten people Reuters spoke to. It marks Algeria's first foreign troop deployment since 1973, when it sent forces to back Egypt in the Arab-Israeli war. Niger is fighting insurgents linked to al-Qaeda and ISIS, and Algeria, which borders Niger, treats Sahel-Sahara stability as a key security priority. Algiers says the move protects its energy and economic interests, including Sonatrach investments and the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline, but has not disclosed the force's size or timetable.

Receives foreign troops amid insurgent threats and military-led rule
Gas pipeline project aims to supply African gas to European markets

Niger's military-led government may gain security support while facing ongoing jihadist threats.

auto-14626a421aff.headline: G20 ministers cancel group photo after Europeans object to Lavrov's presence
auto-14626a421aff.summary:
A planned group photo at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta was dropped after several European delegations declined to pose alongside Russia's foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov. The United States, which is hosting the talks under Secretary of State Marco Rubio, said it chose to skip the picture so the discussions would not become a distraction. Britain confirmed it will not hold direct bilateral engagement with Russian ministers while the war in Ukraine continues. Ukraine was not invited to the meeting.

The report also links the dispute to recent US moves toward Moscow, including the suspension of some sanctions and a deal to import Russian diesel, which Ukraine and European allies have criticised.

actors.why: Lavrov attends, but Moscow is isolated by the photo refusal and sanctions remain.
Hosts the meeting, cancels the photo, and faces criticism over Russia sanctions relief.
Excluded from the meeting and criticises US sanctions relief for Russia.
Refuses direct engagement with Russian ministers, holding a firm position against Moscow.

impact_points: Ukraine is sidelined from the meeting and has criticised Washington's easing of sanctions on Russia.
Russia gains visibility at the forum, while European states and London keep their refusal to engage it directly.

auto-7fc664c10543.headline: Lebanon charges 13 over seized Hezbollah explosives truck
auto-7fc664c10543.summary: A Lebanese military court has charged 13 people in connection with a truck carrying Hezbollah-owned explosives, state media reported. Two suspects remain in custody after the vehicle was stopped at a checkpoint on the highway from Beirut to the Bekaa Valley, while the other 11 were charged in absentia, five of them known only by nicknames. The explosives totalled 780 kilograms, including TNT and C-4. Hezbollah acknowledged owning them, saying they were meant for use against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, and has refused to recognise the government's ban on its military activities.

Hezbollah, its Iran-backed ally, faces setbacks in Lebanon

auto-cc16dd903d09.headline: Houthis reject Saudi claim of drone aimed at Mecca region
auto-cc16dd903d09.summary: Saudi Arabia's coalition in Yemen says it shot down a Houthi drone heading toward the Mecca region on Friday, and earlier intercepted a missile aimed at the west of the kingdom. The Houthis deny targeting Mecca or the surrounding area, saying their cross-border strikes focus on Saudi oil facilities and military sites. Fighting between the Yemeni government, backed by Riyadh, and the Iran-backed Houthis continues along several fronts, including Taiz, where residents face shelling and a siege that limits supplies, according to local reporting. Humanitarian agencies warn conditions for civilians are worsening.

Backs the Houthis, whose escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia are continuing

Civilians in Taiz and other Yemeni fronts face shelling, siege conditions and shortages of water, fuel and medicine.

auto-36ba46917a2d.headline: Carney expects June deal on Canada becoming an EU associate member
auto-36ba46917a2d.summary: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney said he expects to finish negotiations with the European Union in June on a deep partnership that would make Canada the bloc's first associate member. He said he would attend a meeting of European leaders that month to conclude the talks. The arrangement would fall short of full EU membership, but would be the closest relationship the bloc has built with an outside country. The term associate member was not included in a joint declaration that launched the new economic and security alliance.

actors.why: Gains a unprecedented partnership with the EU if June talks conclude
Would establish its closest-ever arrangement with an outside country

impact_points: Canada would gain a closer formal link to the European Union, short of full membership, if the June talks succeed.
The EU would deepen its partnership with Canada, a move that would be unprecedented for an outside country.

auto-9db0d49441fc.headline: Iran's Guard says two tankers burning in Hormuz as Qatar-led talks resume
auto-9db0d49441fc.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on Friday that tankers caught fire and were halted in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings on routes Tehran considers unauthorised. The Guard alleged the ships had switched off tracking systems and were backed by U.S. military support; it gave no names, flags or casualty details. Separately, a small boat reportedly attached explosives to a tanker near Khasab, Oman, causing a fire that was later put out, with no one harmed. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran to push for an end to the Iran-U.S. war, though responsibility for the incidents remains unclear.

Qatari mediators pursuing an agreement between Iran and the United States

UKMTO reported the explosive attack on the tanker and monitors regional shipping

impact_points: Iran faces growing pressure over Hormuz shipping, with its route demands colliding with U.S.-backed navigation.
Oman and shipping operators face security risks, as tankers are hit near its coast and crews are evacuated.

auto-e9e2391fba16.headline: North Korea fires about ten short-range ballistic missiles into the Sea of Japan
auto-e9e2391fba16.summary: North Korea launched around ten short-range ballistic missiles from near Wonsan on its east coast on Thursday, according to South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff, with Japan's Defence Ministry also confirming a launch that landed outside its exclusive economic zone. The firing follows a dispute over landmines that injured three South Korean soldiers in the demilitarised zone in September. A joint South Korea-UN investigation blamed North Korea, which rejected the finding and accused Seoul of fabrication. Pyongyang has also criticised joint US-South Korean air drills and Seoul's offer of military talks, whose outcome remains unclear.

auto-f5e931febd82.headline: Canada and EU unveil Alliance for the Future at Montreal summit
auto-f5e931febd82.summary: Canada and the European Union announced a new partnership called the Alliance for the Future at a summit in Montreal, and said other countries would be welcome to join. Prime Minister Mark Carney and European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen described it as a way to offer stability and opportunity amid climate pressures, democratic strain and trade coercion. Leaders said talks would follow on a more integrated market, easier trade and travel, and student exchanges. They also discussed Canada becoming an associate member of the bloc, though the scope of that role is to be clarified at a 2027 summit. An agreement would give Canada access to European supercomputers for AI work.

auto-3a7656994bb1.headline: US tells non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes
auto-3a7656994bb1.summary:
The United States has ordered its non-emergency government employees and their family members to depart Saudi Arabia, effective October 23, citing safety risks. The US embassy in Riyadh announced the move on Friday and pointed to Houthi missile and drone attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure. Embassy staff now need special authorisation to fly through Saudi airports, and American citizens were warned of possible further attacks, airspace closures and flight cancellations.

The announcement comes as fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's government has grown more intense in recent weeks. The article places this clash within the wider US-Israeli war with Iran, which has opened a new and unstable front.

auto-8d80d0284113.headline: Pakistan's army voices guarded hope over its Iran-US mediation effort
auto-8d80d0284113.summary: Pakistan's military spokesman, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, said the army is cautiously optimistic about its mediation between Iran and the United States. The comment came after Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir made a second trip to Tehran this month, joined on Monday by Saudi and Turkish officials. Chaudhry declined to disclose what was discussed or whether Washington backed the visit, and he pointed to unnamed spoilers who he said benefit from conflict. auto-9ef5f59b6829.headline: Israel demolishes homes of two Palestinians accused in deadly West Bank shooting
auto-9ef5f59b6829.summary: Israeli forces have destroyed the homes of two Palestinian men accused of carrying out a shooting in the occupied West Bank that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three more. Since the attack, a military siege around Hebron has reportedly pushed more than 4,000 residents out of their homes. The reporting describes the demolitions and the displacement; it does not independently confirm the details of the shooting itself.

auto-5d567028cb72.headline: Saudi coalition says it downed Houthi drone aimed at Mecca region
auto-5d567028cb72.summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it shot down a Houthi drone heading toward Mecca's region on Friday morning, according to spokesman Turki al-Malki. It also reported intercepting a cruise missile aimed at western Saudi Arabia earlier that day, and two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh the previous day. A Houthi spokesperson denied targeting Mecca, saying their attacks focus on Saudi oil facilities and military bases. auto-b39a737445e5.headline: Canada and EU pursue closer partnership, including Ukraine loan and minerals deal
auto-b39a737445e5.summary:
Canada and the European Union held a summit in Montreal, where they launched what they call an Alliance for the Future. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney hosted European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa, and the sides signed a digital trade deal along with other agreements. Canada is set to become the bloc's first so-called associate member, a term without legal basis that some EU states dispute.

The two sides also agreed that the European Investment Bank will invest in Canadian critical minerals, pledged AI safety cooperation, and said Canada will contribute 500 million euros to the EU's 90 billion euro Ukraine support loan. They will also negotiate deeper Canadian involvement in the Erasmus+ student exchange programme.

actors.why: Gains closer EU ties, minerals investment and associate member status
Deepens partnership with Canada and funds Ukraine loan, though member states dispute terms
Receives Canadian contribution to the EU's 90 billion euro support loan
Trade dispute with Canada continues while Canada deepens ties with the EU

impact_points: Canada gains closer EU ties, minerals investment and a path to deeper student exchange participation.
EU states that dispute the associate member term may push back on how far the arrangement goes.

auto-74f1e323fd4a.headline: China says new stealth drone completed first takeoff and landing from amphibious ship
auto-74f1e323fd4a.summary: China's state news agency Xinhua reported that the GJ-21, the country's first carrier-based stealth reconnaissance and strike drone, has completed its first takeoff and landing on the Sichuan, the lead vessel of the Type 076 amphibious assault ship class. The trial was described as a breakthrough showing the navy can operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large naval platforms. The GJ-21 first appeared at a Beijing military parade last year marking the 80th anniversary of the end of World War Two. Experts quoted by state media argued the drone is low cost and reusable.

actors.why: Gains a new stealth drone capability from its amphibious assault ship program.
Faces a more capable Chinese naval drone platform in regional waters.

impact_points: China's navy gains a new capability to launch stealth fixed-wing drones from its large amphibious assault ship.
Rival navies in the Asia-Pacific region face a more capable Chinese maritime strike and reconnaissance platform in the South China Sea.

auto-ceecc03f8845.headline: Turkey hosts Libyan rival administrations' talks on reunifying the divided country
auto-ceecc03f8845.summary: Turkey hosted talks in Ankara last week between military officials from Libya's eastern and western administrations, aimed at reunifying the country, a senior Turkish official told AFP. Discussions have so far centred on uniting the armed forces, with political unity expected later, and no agreement has yet been reached, though both sides agreed to keep talking. Turkey's foreign minister Hakan Fidan said conditions were ripe for permanent reunification, hinting an announcement could come soon.

actors.why: Divided state could move toward military and political reunification.
Mediating talks and strengthening its position with both Libyan sides.
Its influence in Libya could diminish under a reunification deal.
Pushing reunification, with Turkish efforts reportedly aligned with its plan.

impact_points: Libya remains split between a UN-recognised Tripoli government and an eastern administration backed by Khalifa Haftar.
Turkey gains influence as mediator, while Russia and some European states could see their influence in Libya diminish.

auto-e8c1c531ec9b.headline: Yemeni government reports missile strikes on Aden airport and palace complex
auto-e8c1c531ec9b.summary: Yemen's government armed forces said on Friday that Houthi forces fired ballistic missiles at Aden airport and the Maashiq presidential palace complex. The military gave no information on casualties, damage, or whether the projectiles reached their targets. A police official told AFP that two missiles were aimed at the presidential palace. Residents in Aden, the base of Yemen's internationally recognised government, reported hearing two explosions late on Friday.

actors.why: Missiles reportedly aimed at Aden airport and presidential palace, the government seat
Saudi Arabia backs Yemen's government and faces rising Houthi hostility nearby
UAE is a regional partner of Yemen's government and may be drawn into tensions

impact_points: Yemen's internationally recognised government faces a direct attack on its seat of power in Aden, with its airport and palace reportedly targeted.
Aden residents and the airport's operations are exposed to danger, and wider regional tensions with the Houthis are likely to deepen.

auto-ca479e35271e.headline: Dockworkers across 22 countries plan Friday strike against Gaza war and arms shipments
auto-ca479e35271e.summary: Dock and port unions in 22 countries are set to hold a coordinated strike on Friday, October 30, under the banner "Dockworkers do not work for war." The action involves more than 110 ports and 25 unions, with some countries, including France, Italy, India, Greece and Turkiye, calling full 24-hour walkouts. The unions demand an immediate end to what they call the genocide of Palestinians and an end to imperialist wars, including US-Israeli operations in the Middle East and against Iran. A campaign group, No Harbour for Genocide, says ports involved have handled weapons-component shipments to Israel, and estimates that over $2bn in cargo could be held up.

actors.why: Strike backs Palestinian demands for an end to genocide and recognition of a state.
Arms-shipment disruption and solidarity action pressure Israel's military supply chain.
Ports at Genoa and Livorno face strikes; USB calls a general strike.
Piraeus port faces 24-hour action; unions there call for wider strikes.
Marseille port and 24-hour strikes disrupt trade and arms-linked shipping.
Tangier port has proven links to weapons shipments and joins two-hour strike.

impact_points: Israel and its arms supply chains face disruption, with ports handling Elbit Systems components expected to be shut for a day.
Ports in Italy, Greece, France and Morocco, which the campaign links to arms shipments, are directly drawn into the labour action.

auto-98ee8c511609.headline: Pakistan cautiously hopeful as mediators seek to revive Iran-US ceasefire
auto-98ee8c511609.summary:
Pakistan's military spokesman, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, said Islamabad's army is cautiously hopeful about mediation between Iran and the United States. Army chief Asim Munir, Pakistan's lead mediator, has travelled to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday with Saudi and Turkish officials. Qatari mediators also arrived in Tehran on Friday, aiming to restore a June ceasefire that later collapsed.

Chaudhry warned that unnamed actors who benefit from conflict are trying to obstruct talks. He declined to disclose what was discussed in Tehran or whether Washington backed the visit. He also said Iran could join the Saudi-Turkish-Pakistani defence pact, while Pakistani troop deployments to Saudi Arabia would depend on political decisions.

Iran faces an ongoing war and is the target of mediation efforts
The United States is a party to the conflict and the mediation talks

impact_points: Iran and the United States face a stalled war, and a revived ceasefire would ease pressure on both.
Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis are fighting again, a clash Pakistan says it is not part of.

auto-b08f86981884.headline: Houthi missiles reportedly aimed at Aden airport and presidential palace
auto-b08f86981884.summary: Yemen's government forces said on Friday that Houthi fighters fired ballistic missiles at Aden airport and the Maashiq Presidential Palace. A military spokesperson accused the group of attacking national infrastructure and said the airport strikes contradicted Houthi claims that they want the blockade lifted. No casualties or damage in Aden were reported in the statements. The same day, the spokesperson said government forces had carried out more than 1,000 attacks on Houthi positions across several fronts, including Taiz, Al-Jawf, Marib and Al-Bayda, as part of the 'Dawn of Yemen' campaign. These claims could not be independently verified.

auto-d0e481fc6415.headline: Israel demolishes homes of Hebron attackers as West Bank operation displaces thousands
auto-d0e481fc6415.summary:
Israeli forces demolished on Friday the homes of two gunmen who killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint in Hebron, in the occupied West Bank, on October 23. The demolitions are part of a wider military operation ordered by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, which has reportedly forced more than 3,000 Palestinians from their homes. Palestinian officials accuse Netanyahu of using the operation to build support before Israel's election on Tuesday, while Israel says it is responding to the attack.

The military has also reportedly demolished other homes, shops, roads and factories in Hebron and closed most entrances to the city, restricting movement for Palestinians. UN human rights chief Volker Türk warned of possible disproportionate force and ethnic cleansing.

actors.why: Thousands displaced, homes and businesses demolished, movement severely restricted in Hebron.

impact_points: Palestinian residents of Hebron face displacement, home losses and restricted movement, including access to medical care.

auto-967e99796cec.headline: Lebanese military prosecutors charge 13 over seized explosives shipment linked to Hezbollah
auto-967e99796cec.summary:
Lebanese military prosecutors have charged 13 people, several of them Hezbollah members, over a shipment of about 800 kilograms of C-4 and TNT seized this month at a checkpoint in Dahr Al-Baidar. The suspects face charges including belonging to unauthorised armed factions and undermining state authority. Officials say the shipment was part of an organised network, and the case will now go to a military investigating judge who may issue arrest warrants.

Hezbollah has pressed for the explosives to be returned and its lawmakers called the charges politically motivated. A request by the justice minister and a parliamentary bloc to move the case to a civilian court is still awaiting a Cabinet decision.

actors.why: State asserts authority over armed factions; charges signal judicial escalation against Hezbollah
A Russian national is named as a suspect, married to a detained Hezbollah member

impact_points: Lebanon's state faces a major test of its authority over Hezbollah and other armed groups.
Hezbollah is under judicial and political pressure, with members charged and its weapons activities contested.

auto-8fe699d259bd.headline: European diplomats snub G20 family photo over Russian foreign minister's presence
auto-8fe699d259bd.summary: At a G20 foreign ministers' meeting hosted by the United States in Atlanta, European diplomats declined to pose for the traditional group photo alongside Russia's foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, so the US cancelled it. The UK's foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, confronted Lavrov directly, blaming Moscow for the war in Ukraine and urging members to increase economic and diplomatic pressure on Russia. Ukraine was not invited to the meeting, and the piece notes that US-Russia ties have partly warmed even as Kyiv and its European partners criticise Washington's easing of some Russian sanctions.

auto-886394b91240.headline: Iran's Guards say three oil tankers hit in Hormuz; Oman rescues crew
auto-886394b91240.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps said three oil tankers were halted in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting to use routes it had not authorised, with one described as a supertanker that caught fire. The Guards attributed the stoppages to incidents or mines; the claims could not be independently verified. Oman's Maritime Security Centre said it evacuated 25 crew from a burning crude tanker, the RITI, flying the Panamanian flag, though it was unclear whether that ship was among the three. The US military denied the mine claims and said main transit routes had been cleared.

auto-c6deacf429c0.headline: Africans recruited into Russia's war in Ukraine; Tunisian families seek missing men
auto-c6deacf429c0.summary: A France 24 video report says more than 1,400 Africans have been enlisted by Russia since 2023 to fight in Ukraine. The recruitment was not on the agenda at an Africa-Russia summit where African leaders and Russian officials discussed security, trade and political ties. The report focuses on Tunisia, where relatives of several men who went to Russia for work or study are still trying to learn what happened to them.

actors.why: Families of missing men seeking answers about their fate.

African nations more broadly face scrutiny as citizens are drawn into a foreign war through recruitment.

auto-3dbe99e74826.summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it shot down a Houthi drone heading toward the Mecca region on Friday morning, spokesman Turki al-Malki announced on social media. Fighting along front lines in Yemen, including around Taiz, continued, and aid agencies warned of worsening conditions for civilians.

auto-e4fa67810ac2.headline: Rubio urges G20 unity as Lavrov's attendance strains Atlanta meeting
auto-e4fa67810ac2.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted G20 officials in Atlanta and called on members to cooperate in addressing threats to the global economic system. auto-3bb5fb0b271c.headline: Lula confirms attendance at COP31 climate talks in Antalya
auto-3bb5fb0b271c.summary: Brazil's presidency said President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva will attend the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. He is due to arrive on November 10 for the leaders' segment on November 11 and 12, part of the annual UN climate negotiations. The announcement came shortly after his recent re-election. Lula will then travel to the Philippines on November 13 for an ASEAN summit, his second consecutive invitation to that gathering. Seventy-seven heads of state and government have so far confirmed participation, and Britain's prime minister is also expected to attend.

auto-0c81c9443e7f.headline: Eight-year-old Palestinian boy dies after Israeli fire in southern Gaza
auto-0c81c9443e7f.summary: An eight-year-old Palestinian boy, Yamen Hisham Yahya Saqr, died on Friday from wounds he received when Israeli forces opened fire in the Qizan Rashwan area south of Khan Younis. He had been shot on Wednesday, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. Separately, Gaza's civil defence crews recovered the body of a 47-year-old man from the al-Waha area north of Gaza City, who Wafa said was killed in an Israeli air strike three days earlier. The report also describes Israeli drone bombing south of Khan Younis and heavy military fire east of Hamad City on Wednesday.
