auto-cb82392e945e.headline: UN names Russian envoy to oversee mine clearance amid Ukraine criticism
auto-cb82392e945e.summary:
The United Nations has appointed Gleb Desyatnikov, Russia's ambassador to Jordan since 2018, as assistant secretary-general for mine action and police. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres announced the post on October 27. Ukraine's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi condemned the choice, saying it undermines trust in the UN, since Ukraine is working to clear large numbers of Russian-laid mines.

Authorities in Kherson region said demining teams have neutralised over 300,000 explosive devices on the right bank and cleared 74.5% of the designated area. Human Rights Watch has said Russia used many anti-personnel and anti-vehicle mine models, with about 30% of Ukraine contaminated.

auto-86f773d38db5.headline: Poland's top court leadership ousted amid sharp dispute between Tusk and president
auto-86f773d38db5.summary: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal was thrown into crisis on Friday after a judge suspended its nationalist-linked president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy for a month and declared herself in charge. Święczkowski rejected the move and called it a coup, while his deputy was refused entry to the building. Protesters clashed with police outside, and former ruling party leader Jarosław Kaczyński demanded presidential intervention. The dispute centres on Prime Minister Donald Tusk's effort to reverse judicial changes made under the Law and Justice government, with the court's makeup and the question of which judges may hear cases now contested.

auto-8d13b02d3641.headline: Hundreds leave occupied Oleshky during brief humanitarian ceasefire window
auto-8d13b02d3641.summary: Hundreds of residents were evacuated from Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city in Ukraine, on Friday during a short humanitarian pause. The truce was reportedly brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump and gave civilians a four-hour window to leave. auto-c214f174152b.headline: Pyongyang rejects sanctions as a means of curbing its nuclear status
auto-c214f174152b.summary: North Korea has argued that international sanctions cannot strip it of its standing as a nuclear-armed state. auto-bd6b296e7b34.headline: Brazil calls in Argentine envoy over Flavio Bolsonaro's departure to the US
auto-bd6b296e7b34.summary: Brazil's Foreign Ministry has summoned Argentina's chargé d'affaires, Maria Emilia Cortes, to seek explanations about Flavio Bolsonaro's exit from Brazil. auto-d639ade6c17a.headline: Opinion piece warns of renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran after lull
auto-d639ade6c17a.summary:

auto-7ab0472ced4e.headline: Saudi coalition says it downed Houthi drone; Houthis reject claim of targeting Medina
auto-7ab0472ced4e.summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone on Friday morning that was heading toward the Mecca region, and that a cruise missile aimed at western Saudi Arabia had also been shot down. auto-6234748ec913.summary:
Switzerland's foreign minister Ignazio Cassis ended a two-day visit to North Korea, the first by a Swiss government minister in over twenty years. He met Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui and party secretary Jo Yong Won, and discussed restoring political relations and renewing dialogue, as well as security on the Korean Peninsula and wider Eurasian challenges. Bern also reopened its diplomatic office in Pyongyang, which operates without an ambassador and reports to the Swiss embassy in Beijing. Reports did not confirm any meeting with leader Kim Jong Un.

Cassis then travelled to Seoul for talks on peninsula security and easing tensions. Separately, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz referred to his own country's reunification during a visit to the inter-Korean border.

auto-523537fc6ca4.headline: UAE halts tanker oil leak as coastal cleanup and beach closures continue
auto-523537fc6ca4.summary: The United Arab Emirates says a leak from the tanker Gem No. 2 has been stopped and no new spillage has been detected. The launch follows a landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone that injured three South Korean soldiers in September, which a joint investigation blamed on North Korea; Pyongyang rejected that finding and accused Seoul of fabrication.

The firing came days after Seoul proposed military talks to restore communication channels, and as South Korea and US air forces conduct drills. It is unclear whether Pyongyang will accept talks.

The attack was reported by the Palestinian news agency Wafa and the Quds News Network, citing Gaza's civil defence agency. The report does not establish any military justification for the strike.

auto-3dd609f53bf5.headline: Rival Western Sahara resolutions both fail at UN Security Council
auto-3dd609f53bf5.summary: Two competing draft resolutions on Western Sahara, one put forward by the United States and one by Russia, were both voted down in the UN Security Council. The outcome leaves the council without a consensus text on the disputed territory's future. Neither draft secured the votes needed for adoption, and the result reflects the continuing split between Washington and Moscow over the issue.

auto-25db74d1122d.headline: Saudi coalition reports intercepting Houthi drone and missiles; Houthis deny targeting Medina
auto-25db74d1122d.summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it destroyed a Houthi drone heading toward Saudi Arabia's Mecca region on Friday morning, and that it had also downed a cruise missile aimed at the west of the kingdom. The coalition spokesman, Turki al-Malki, made the claims on social media, and the Houthis denied targeting the holy city or its surroundings, saying their cross-border strikes hit Saudi energy and military sites. Fighting between Yemen's Riyadh-backed government and the Iran-backed Houthis continued on several fronts, including Taiz, where civilians face shelling and a siege, according to Al Jazeera's reporting from the city.

auto-6f96b6652d43.headline: Lavrov objects to Poland's G20 invitation as European diplomats snub joint photo
auto-6f96b6652d43.summary:
Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said that inviting Poland to a G20 meeting breaks diplomatic rules. The gathering of foreign ministers, hosted by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Atlanta, was overshadowed by a dispute over a planned group photograph. European diplomats reportedly refused to pose with Lavrov, and the US cancelled the picture. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband confronted Lavrov directly, blaming Russia for the war in Ukraine and urging more economic pressure on Moscow.

The article also notes a partial thaw in US-Russia relations, with Washington waiving some sanctions and approving a deal to import Russian diesel, while Ukraine and European allies have criticised the move.

auto-78239294763b.headline: Russian satellite closes in on Ukrainian-used Finnish-American imaging satellite
auto-78239294763b.summary:
A Russian military satellite, Cosmos-2612, changed its orbit in mid-October 2026 and drew within about a kilometre of Iceye-X36, a commercial radar imaging satellite built by Finland's Iceye and used to supply images to Ukraine's armed forces. The US State Department called the manoeuvre threatening and linked it to in-orbit military operations. Analysts at the French firm Aldoria said the approach used a lot of fuel but was a first of its kind, and that it may be aimed at pressuring Ukraine by disrupting imaging schedules. No debris was seen, so the satellite does not appear to have been struck.

The closeness of the approach, shown by tracking data and a satellite imagery company's photo, is the key detail, though the intent behind it could not be confirmed.

Its satellite carried out a pressure manoeuvre against a rival's asset

auto-8760b9ee1ca8.headline: Kyiv reportedly halts refinery strikes under US pressure
auto-8760b9ee1ca8.summary: Ukraine's military has reportedly paused its long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries, following pressure from US President Donald Trump, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing people familiar with the operations. Ukrainian units were reportedly told in mid-October that the campaign was effectively on hold once missions already underway were finished, with the pause possibly lasting past the US midterm elections. Reuters could not immediately verify the account, which comes as US-backed efforts to revive peace talks with Russia gather pace.

Refinery strikes paused while Russia intensifies attacks on Ukrainian energy
Trump's pressure secured a pause and reflects his push for peace talks

impact_points: Ukraine faces a possible loss of its main long-range pressure on Russian energy, with Kyiv earlier calling drones its only viable response.
Russia, meanwhile, has reportedly stepped up attacks on Ukrainian energy and civilian infrastructure, while Washington's strained ties with Kyiv deepen.

auto-d197d04b8d63.headline: Ukraine reports 1,670 more Russian casualties in one day
auto-d197d04b8d63.summary: Ukraine's General Staff says Russian forces suffered 1,670 personnel losses, counting killed and wounded, over the previous 24 hours. The cumulative total since late February 2022 now stands at 1,588,170, according to the figures posted on the General Staff's Facebook page. The report also lists equipment losses, including artillery systems. The figures are Ukrainian military claims and have not been independently verified.

actors.why: Reports heavy daily personnel and artillery losses during the ongoing war.
Publishes casualty claims highlighting battlefield attrition against Russian forces.

impact_points: Russia is absorbing heavy personnel and equipment losses as its war against Ukraine continues.
Ukraine uses these daily tallies to publicly track the scale of Russian casualties and battlefield attrition.

auto-735dd236076b.headline: Strike on Kyiv energy site cuts power and water in several districts
auto-735dd236076b.summary: Russian forces struck an energy facility in Kyiv on the evening of 30 October, according to Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko and the private utility DTEK. Parts of four districts, Obolonskyi, Darnytskyi, Desnianskyi and Podilskyi, lost electricity, and DTEK said scheduled rolling outages were not in effect there. Klitschko later said three drones hit a critical infrastructure site, and the resulting power loss lowered water pressure across the city. Water was restored in Obolonskyi, while several other districts still faced reduced pressure or no water. Crews were working on repairs, and windows were damaged in a residential building in Shevchenkivskyi, with no fire reported.

Its forces carried out the strike on Kyiv's infrastructure

impact_points: Kyiv residents face loss of power and water across several districts, with repairs still underway.
Ukraine's energy system and city infrastructure absorb further damage from the strike, adding strain to utility crews.

auto-fba2ad302161.headline: Brazil summons Argentine envoy over Flavio Bolsonaro's exit to the United States
auto-fba2ad302161.summary:
Brazil's foreign ministry has reportedly called in Argentina's chargé d'affaires to ask about the role Buenos Aires played in helping Flavio Bolsonaro leave Brazil after losing the presidential runoff. Argentina's foreign minister Pablo Quirno has publicly denied receiving any formal request for explanations. Bolsonaro, who is under investigation in a money-laundering probe linked to Banco Master, reached Miami after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador, and has refused to concede defeat to President Lula, who won with 51.8 percent.

The episode adds strain to already tense ties between Lula and Argentina's President Javier Milei, which had seen both countries recall their ambassadors in August. Milei's spokesperson described the trip as a rescue, while Bolsonaro thanked Milei for unspecified help.

impact_points: Brazil faces a further diplomatic rift with Argentina, with Lula's government seeking answers over Bolsonaro's departure.
Argentina risks worsening tensions with Brazil and its own standing, as Milei's government is accused of aiding a politician under investigation.

auto-d23244bad41f.headline: Pakistan's army voices guarded hope over its Iran-US mediation role
auto-d23244bad41f.summary:
Pakistan's military spokesman, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, said the army is cautiously optimistic about its efforts to mediate between Iran and the United States. He pointed to the repeated trips to Tehran by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, the latest on Monday with Saudi and Turkish officials, as a sign of progress. Chaudhry declined to say what was discussed or whether Washington backed the visits, and warned of unnamed spoilers who benefit from conflict.

The spokesman also addressed the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August, and said Iran could be welcome to join. Iran's security council secretary had earlier called for regional security without foreign intervention.

auto-aa7b3d5ec208.headline: Russia launches 134 drones at Ukraine overnight, hitting 20 sites
auto-aa7b3d5ec208.summary: Russian forces sent 134 drones of several types, including Shahed, Gerbera and decoy models, against Ukraine during the night of 30 to 31 October. According to Ukraine's Air Force, 72 of the Shaheds were jet-powered. By 08:30, Ukrainian air defences had destroyed or jammed 105 of the drones, 49 of them jet-powered Shaheds. Strikes hit 20 locations, and falling debris was reported at 10 more. Several drones were still airborne and fighting was ongoing. Separately, a drone struck a house in Kharkiv, injuring five people.

impact_points: Ukraine faces continued drone strikes on civilian and infrastructure sites, with five injured in Kharkiv.

auto-5b996fdd04a0.headline: Ukraine's military says Russia has lost over 1.5 million troops since 2022
auto-5b996fdd04a0.summary: Ukraine's General Staff reported on October 31 that Russian forces have suffered about 1,588,180 casualties since the full-scale invasion began in February 2022. The figure includes 1,670 losses recorded in the previous day, and the report also lists large numbers of tanks, armored vehicles, artillery systems and aircraft destroyed or lost. Ukraine does not publish its own losses, citing operational secrecy. Western think-tank CSIS estimates Russian casualties run roughly two to two-and-a-half times higher than Ukraine's, while President Zelensky said in February that at least 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers had been killed.

actors.why: Reported losses of troops and equipment mount heavily against Russian forces
Ukraine has suffered heavy casualties and struggles to recover its dead

impact_points: Russia faces mounting personnel and equipment losses after more than three and a half years of fighting.
Ukraine is affected by heavy casualties and difficulties recovering the bodies of fallen soldiers under drone fire.

auto-ee15dbfc95c5.headline: Ghana and Russia discuss nuclear plant and bauxite mining deals
auto-ee15dbfc95c5.summary: Ghana has opened talks with Russia's state nuclear agency, Rosatom, about building the country's first nuclear power station, according to Ghanaian media. The talks followed a bilateral meeting between Presidents Vladimir Putin and John Dramani Mahama on the sidelines of a Russia-Africa summit in Moscow. Separately, Russian aluminium producer Rusal signed agreements with Ghana's state aluminium development corporation to mine bauxite at the Nyinahin deposit in the Ashanti Region, with the site said to hold over 100 million tonnes, and to build an alumina refinery.

impact_points: Ghana would gain a potential new power source and a diversified energy mix, as its President has signalled.
Russia gains a foothold in Ghana's mining and nuclear sectors while seeking partners beyond Western sanctions.

auto-d5407699525e.headline: Russian attacks on Zaporizhzhia Oblast leave one dead, two hurt in a day
auto-d5407699525e.summary: Russian forces carried out 935 attacks across 51 settlements in Zaporizhzhia Oblast over the past day, according to Ivan Fedorov, co-chair of the regional defence council, who posted the figures on social media. The assaults combined airstrikes, roughly 745 drones, mostly FPV models, and about 175 artillery strikes. One person was killed and two were injured, and officials logged 69 reports of damage to homes, vehicles and infrastructure. Targets included the regional capital and numerous towns and villages across the oblast.

auto-5b93c184b640.summary: Oil tankers were reportedly hit in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing Iran war, according to the live coverage's headline. auto-3033361fd002.summary: US President Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that discussions with Iran are continuing and that Tehran wants to keep talking. auto-8657e9fa9218.headline: US clears $2.1bn sale of 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine
auto-8657e9fa9218.summary: The United States has signed off on a sale of 500 Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine, valued at $2.1 billion. The State Department said European allies and Canada would fund the purchase, with Germany, Canada and Norway providing donations alongside Ukrainian national funds and an EU loan. President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed the approval but warned that deliveries could take several years, and he has pressed for faster release of the weapons as Russia steps up strikes on Ukraine's power grid. The missiles are reportedly new production amid a global shortage linked to US use in its war with Iran.

auto-ca53ef325491.headline: Black Sea wildlife toll rises as war damages marine environment
auto-ca53ef325491.summary: Researchers say ongoing fighting in the Black Sea region has killed a large number of dolphins, with one Ukrainian scientist estimating more than 120,000 deaths by 2026, roughly a quarter of the sea's cetaceans. Explosions, missile launches and military sonar are said to disorient the animals, leaving them unable to hunt or navigate, while pollution from sunken warships and tankers adds to the damage. Officials and researchers across the littoral states report rising deaths, though causes are hard to confirm because most carcasses are decomposed. Russian monitors blamed the deaths on parasites and viruses without detailed explanation.

auto-3037631a0f36.headline: Doubts grow over Venezuela oilfield deal's promised output surge
auto-3037631a0f36.summary: A deal Washington has described as the largest oil transaction in history would hand 17 Venezuelan oilfields, reportedly holding about 64 billion barrels, to one company. That firm, North American Blue Energy Partners, is led by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt, who until recently was the subject of U.S. money-laundering inquiries involving funds taken from state oil company PDVSA. Under the arrangement the United States would take a 35% stake in the parent company and gain the right to buy 20% of output at production cost. The company says it will raise output from about 224,000 barrels a day in mid-October to more than 1 million.

auto-110d74360389.headline: Evacuees from Russian-held Oleshky fly to Belarus en route to Ukraine
auto-110d74360389.summary: Three flights carrying residents evacuated from Oleshky, a Ukrainian city under Russian control near the front line, landed at Gomel airport in Belarus, according to the Belarusian state news agency Belta. Those who chose to go to Ukraine travelled by bus through Crimea to the Russian town of Anapa before flying on, and they are expected to cross into Ukraine at a border point. The evacuation, carried out as a joint relief operation by the warring sides during a days-long ceasefire, is described as the first of its kind in the nearly five-year war. Around 200 residents were reported to have left for Ukraine, while dozens more opted to travel into Russian territory.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty told a security summit in Bahrain that he is deeply concerned a fresh round of fighting between the United States and Iran would be more destructive and lead nowhere. Iran has proposed lifting the US blockade of its ports in return for reopening the waterway within a week. Qatari mediators went back to Tehran, but the two sides still disagree on whether nuclear talks or easing of the blockade and oil sanctions should come first.

The same report also covers Lebanon, where Prime Minister Nawaf Salam has opened consultations on a plan to govern the country's 12 Palestinian refugee camps, which currently involve overlapping authority among factions, state bodies and UNRWA.

auto-f5ba98f1e8ec.headline: Ethiopian drone strikes reportedly kill at least 25 civilians in north
auto-f5ba98f1e8ec.summary: Multiple drone strikes in northern Ethiopia since Thursday have reportedly killed at least 25 civilians, including children, according to witnesses and a medical source cited by AFP. Four strikes reportedly hit a camp for displaced people in Amhara, about 400 kilometres northeast of Addis Ababa, as students were heading home from school. A further strike in Tigray reportedly hit a lorry carrying grain, then struck people gathering the spilled grain, killing at least 11. The Ethiopian army did not respond to requests for comment, and the death tolls could not be independently confirmed.

auto-02383331b974.headline: Drone strike sets fire to Ufa refinery, damaging key processing unit
auto-02383331b974.summary: Drones struck Ufa, the capital of Bashkortostan in Russia, overnight on 30-31 October, sparking a fire at the Bashneft-Novoil refinery. Citing eyewitness photos, an analyst for the Russian outlet Astra believes the L-35 catalytic reforming unit, which makes high-octane petrol components and hydrogen used to clean fuel, is the part on fire. Analysts quoted in the piece say Gaza and the West Bank barely influenced voters because both blocs largely agreed on policy there, with domestic issues such as judicial power and ultra-Orthodox military exemptions dominating. Commentators also argue many Israelis are aware of Gaza's devastation yet fail to grapple with its moral implications.

auto-354675cc56cb.summary: Authorities in France and Germany are preparing for possible unrest as a large number of demonstrations have been called across both countries. Organisers have scheduled hundreds of rallies, prompting police and officials to plan for heavy security. The reporting available does not confirm the precise causes or the scale of any disorder that may follow.

auto-0827a79a2381.headline: Ukrainian drone-launched net reportedly used to capture and kill Russian soldier
auto-0827a79a2381.summary: Ukraine's military reportedly used a drone-mounted net launcher against a Russian infantryman on the front line, according to the manufacturer Ptashka Drones. After a first FPV drone strike missed, a second drone dropped a net that trapped the soldier, who could not free himself. Soldiers from the 3rd Assault Brigade then killed him with FPV drones. The company says its net cartridges cost roughly $27 to $33 each, and the launcher is reusable against FPV drones. The company's claims were not independently verified.

auto-adbb8cf60ede.headline: Ukraine accuses Russia of using Oleshky truce to rearm and frame Kyiv's forces
auto-adbb8cf60ede.summary: Ukraine's Pivden Group of Forces says it is observing a local humanitarian ceasefire around Oleshky, a town in occupied Kherson Oblast, while Russian units use the pause to rotate troops, reinforce positions and bring in ammunition. Spokesperson Maksym Kravchuk said Ukrainian units have spotted Russian reconnaissance drones and recorded munitions dropped from drones, which he described as an attempt to portray Ukraine as breaking the agreement. He said the truce exists to evacuate civilians to Ukrainian-controlled territory. These claims come from the Ukrainian side and could not be independently verified.

auto-dc8e142d8895.headline: Iran's foreign minister calls US outreach encouraging but sees no meetings yet
auto-dc8e142d8895.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said a US effort to open dialogue is a constructive move, but said Tehran has no plans to meet American officials at this stage. He said Iran had reviewed a letter from US Vice President JD Vance and laid out conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. An Iranian delegation has gone to Doha after Qatari mediators visited Tehran to try to revive the US-Iran ceasefire. Araghchi said the conditions include lifting sanctions, reducing US forces in the region, restoring oil waivers and releasing frozen funds, and he warned that Iran is prepared for a possible attack.

auto-78e9e54bfe34.headline: Ethiopia's prime minister has ministers train with the military
auto-78e9e54bfe34.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has had his cabinet ministers and other senior officials take part in military training at the Hurso centre. Photos he posted online show him joining exercises alongside ministers, deputy ministers and institution heads. The start date and planned length of the programme were not clear. Abiy said that military discipline could help produce capable, unified leaders who can support national development. The training happens while Ethiopia faces fighting in Tigray, conflict in Amhara and insecurity in Oromia, as well as tensions with neighbouring Eritrea.

auto-75df3843ccc7.headline: Oleshky residents evacuated under short local truce in occupied Kherson region
auto-75df3843ccc7.summary:
Hundreds of residents of Oleshky, a heavily damaged city under Russian occupation, have been evacuated after a humanitarian ceasefire brokered with help from US First Lady Melania Trump, Russian and Ukrainian officials said. Planes carried evacuees to Gomel in Belarus, and buses were due to take them on to Ukraine's Chernihiv region. Many residents chose to stay despite severe shortages of power, gas and water.

The truce covers the Kherson frontline and is set to run until the end of Sunday 1 November. Residents fear Russia may use the pause to strengthen its positions along the Dnipro river, and the Kremlin has said the deal should not be read as a willingness to extend the truce.

auto-b3cf96185e63.headline: Police arrest protesters at London rally against Palestine Action ban
auto-b3cf96185e63.summary: Police in London began making arrests at a demonstration outside the US embassy in Battersea, south London, where more than 100 people gathered to protest the proscription of Palestine Action. Demonstrators carried signs expressing opposition to genocide and support for the banned group. A similar protest was planned for the US consulate near Holyrood in Edinburgh. Before the event, the Metropolitan Police warned attendees they could be arrested, and Commander Adam Slonecki said that supporting a proscribed organisation is unlawful, with those helping organise facing possible enforcement action. Defend Our Juries, which organised the protests, accused the force of being concerned about embarrassing the United States.

auto-8c7ef11c4aa0.headline: Oil flows from the Gulf recover, yet prices keep climbing amid Iran war risks
auto-8c7ef11c4aa0.summary:
Crude exports from the Gulf rose to about 24.6 million barrels per day in the week to October 18, above the pre-war average, according to the market intelligence firm Kpler. Despite this, Brent crude climbed to its highest level since April, trading above $117 a barrel, as traders worry about renewed fighting in the conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran.

Analysts cited shipping risks in the Strait of Hormuz, depleted stockpiles and sharply higher freight costs as drivers of the rise. Producers have shifted more exports to bypass the strait, while the IEA says output remains well below its pre-war baseline.

auto-cf82c66b3bd8.summary: Hundreds of residents of Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city in Ukraine's Kherson region, have been evacuated during a short humanitarian ceasefire, Russian and Ukrainian officials said. auto-50c104c6dc04.headline: Houthi forces claim missile and drone strikes on Saudi energy and airport sites
auto-50c104c6dc04.summary: Yemen's Houthi armed forces said they carried out six attacks on targets inside Saudi Arabia, using ballistic missiles and drones. The group said the strikes responded to Saudi attacks that it said killed women and children in Yemen, and it vowed further operations until the blockade of Yemen ends. Writing in The Guardian ahead of a Commonwealth summit in the Caribbean, he called the trade a brutal violation and proposed structured dialogue with affected communities. He also said he would back a debt restructuring push, led by Gordon Brown, for the poorest Commonwealth states. auto-743e81ffc23e.headline: UAE nominee places fourth in first UN Security Council straw poll
auto-743e81ffc23e.summary: Lana Nusseibeh, the United Arab Emirates' candidate for UN Secretary-General, finished fourth in an informal Security Council straw poll on Friday, receiving seven encourage votes, six discourage votes and two no-opinion votes. Ballots were cast on plain paper, so it is unclear whether any permanent member opposed her. Candidates need at least nine favourable votes and no veto from a permanent member to advance to the General Assembly. Nusseibeh, a long-serving Emirati diplomat nominated late in October, faces criticism from rights groups and Sudan's UN mission over UAE policy in Sudan's civil war. Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan led the poll, and Turkey formally nominated Feridun Sinirlioglu shortly after the vote.

auto-cee10deb2c00.headline: US clears $2.1bn Patriot interceptor sale for Ukraine, with delivery years away

Officials said Kyiv would pay using funds from Canada, Germany and Norway through a US programme, plus money from the European Union's Ukraine Support Loan. Because the missiles have not yet been built, two people briefed on the decision expected deliveries not to arrive until the early 2030s. The approval follows weeks of waiting by Kyiv as Russian strikes on energy and civilian sites intensified.

auto-0b446b2d3f78.headline: El Salvador deploys 2,000 troops to Haiti amid gang violence
auto-0b446b2d3f78.summary:
El Salvador has sent around 2,000 soldiers to Haiti, where they were seen in a convoy of armoured vehicles in Port-au-Prince's Tabarre district. The deployment followed an attack by gangs that left four Salvadoran members of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force missing. Haiti's government says the four were abducted, and President Nayib Bukele has said his priority is bringing them home, while insisting his country is not invading Haiti. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and experts have questioned the troops' exact role and whether they could escalate violence.

Social media posts from gang leaders have threatened to outgun the Salvadoran forces. The UN says more than 5,700 people were killed or wounded in Haiti between January and mid-September.

auto-6f37fbcf1c68.summary: Moldova's military reported that an unauthorised drone entered its airspace on Saturday, 31 October, while Russia was carrying out large-scale air attacks on Ukraine. Moldova's Air Operations Centre said the object was first detected at 16:24 travelling from a Ukrainian village in Odesa Oblast toward Plopi in the Rîbnița district of Transnistria, the breakaway region. It was later seen near Bănești and then disappeared from radar near Țibirica at 16:54. Authorities imposed temporary airspace restrictions over northern and central Moldova and asked residents not to approach any suspicious aircraft or debris and to call 112.
